papers.summary: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom behaviour, compatible with observations. The exact dark energy-free framework needs a single closure condition that we implement in terms of parametrizations of the 3-years data of the DESI team. The resulting redshift dependence of effective cosmological characteristics is then illustrated and subject to physical interpretation. The aim of this paper is to set a benchmark that has to be met by any structure formation model or simulation investigated within general relativity in a flow-orthogonal foliation of spacetime, given the hypothesis.

papers.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
papers.summary: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.

papers.title: SurgeCount: A Protocol-Guided Composition Harness for Bimanual Surgical Sponge Counting
papers.summary: We present SurgeCount, a system for auditable robotic surgical sponge counting that composes learned skills under a written procedural protocol. Retained sponges cause preventable harm, and surgical teams count every sponge before closure to reduce that risk. The robot repeatedly isolates one deformable sponge from a tangled pile and places it in the next numbered counting-tray slot, requiring handling of occluded grasp threads while preserving step order. We train one subtask-conditioned policy on eleven short skills and learn when each skill ends. At each learned boundary, a stateful vision-language model selects the next skill from an operator-authored specification of step order, visual verification, and recovery. This creates temporal commitment to each subtask and enables failures to be recovered by recomposing existing skills rather than using a dedicated recovery policy. We evaluate five methods across 100 real-robot trials using 20 matched layouts. SurgeCount fills 47 of 60 ordered slots and completes 12 of 20 procedures, compared with 27 of 60 and 3 of 20 for the strongest of four end-to-end policies trained on the same data. Replacing the detailed protocol prompt with a minimal prompt reduces performance to 29 of 60 slots and 5 of 20 completed procedures. These results show that long-horizon performance depends not only on visuomotor capacity, but also on how learned skills are committed, verified, and composed. This tabletop proof of concept motivates further evaluation of protocol-guided robotic sponge counting in clinically representative settings.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the Findings Track of Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026

papers.title: Déjà VAE: When Do Autoencoder Traces Reveal Generated Images?
papers.summary: A latent diffusion model's output has already passed through its autoencoder, so a second round trip changes it very little. This "déjà vu" underlies reconstruction-based detectors of generated images; we analyse when it reveals a generated image and when it does not. Read by a frozen vision foundation model without training, the trace is strongest in intermediate layers, and, unlike pixel-level reconstruction error, it treats blur as a sign of a real image. It belongs to the generator's exact decoder: on Synthbuster, the exact decoders of Stable Diffusion 1.3, 1.4, 2 and XL are the strongest of eight autoencoders and catch 94-100% of their generators' images at a 5% false-alarm rate (SDXL's version identified post hoc), while near-identical versions catch 7-42%. A detector trained only on real photographs and their autoencoder copies matches one trained on 162k generated images on GenImage (+2.3 points, 95% CI [0.9, 3.7]) and complements it in fusion, but one resize with JPEG re-save, or a mild blur, costs it 19-27 points. Two lessons concern benchmarks. The in-the-wild benchmark Chameleon can be solved from image width alone. And on Synthbuster, how the real photographs are matched to the generated images' size decides whether our detector leads or trails (+4.4 or -9.7 points): the matching protocol alone can reverse a detector comparison. Code and per-image scores: https://github.com/iamsaugatpandey/deja-vae
papers.comment: 29 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables. Code and per-image scores: https://github.com/iamsaugatpandey/deja-vae

papers.title: Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid
papers.summary: We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $ω$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $ω=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents. The photon sphere is unstable for all values of $ω$ and $N$ considered. Its instability weakens with increasing $N$ for $ω\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $N$ for $ω=1/3$ and strengthens for $ω=1$. For $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the ISCO and the OSCO, which merge at a critical value of $N$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. In contrast, for $ω\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the ISCO, whose location varies with $N$. We also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent $(λ_t^T)^2$, valid for arbitrary $ω$, whose sign changes exactly at the ISCO and OSCO, so that the Lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. The Schwarzschild--de Sitter, mass-shifted Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 12 figures, 6 tables, comments are welcome

papers.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
papers.summary: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

papers.title: LeIFF: A localized-electron and ion force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics
papers.summary: Classical and machine-learned interatomic potentials enable large-scale simulations by replacing electronic structure with an effective energy surface for nuclear motion. This excludes electronic dynamics, electronic excitation and energy exchange between electrons and ions. First-principles electron dynamics can describe these processes, but its computational cost restricts system sizes and simulation times. Electron force fields offer an intermediate description by treating electrons as semiclassical dynamical particles interacting with ions. We introduce the localized-electron and ion force field (LeIFF), a compact physical model for both ground state bonding and excited electron dynamics. Valence electrons are represented by spin-labeled spherical charge distributions with dynamical centers and widths. The energy combines analytic electronic kinetic, Coulomb, and dispersion terms with spline-interpolated short-range interactions fitted to a large molecular data set. The resulting energy surface describes a variety of ground state properties across diverse bonding environments and charge states. It also provides a qualitative description of electronic behavior away from equilibrium. It shows improved robustness, accuracy, and transferability relative to earlier electron force-fields. Without any solid-state training, the same model describes dielectric screening and collective electronic response in silicon. LeIFF thus opens a route to large-scale simulations of nonadiabatic processes in molecules and solids, combining chemical bonding and nonequilibrium electronic motion within a common physical framework.
papers.comment: Main text: 21 pages (including references), 13 figures, 3 tables; Supplementary Information: 22 pages, 26 figures, 3 tables

papers.title: Hydrodynamic interactions of self-propelled tandem flappers with passive pitching
papers.summary: We simulate two in-line, self-propelled 3D flappers of finite span, driven by sinusoidal heaving motions with a phase difference $Δφ$. Pitching is passive, governed by fluid--structure interaction and resisted by a torsional spring. We first consider identical spring stiffnesses, set to the value that maximises the propulsive speed of an isolated flapper. We characterise the self-arrangement of the pair. The pair settles into a stable equilibrium for all phase shifts, travelling at a common propulsive speed and maintaining an equilibrium distance that increases approximately linearly with $Δφ$. The leader is largely unaffected by the presence of the follower and performs similarly to an isolated flapper, whereas the follower requires more power in every case. This additional power outweighs the small increase in propulsive speed, so that the tandem generally provides no efficiency benefit over an isolated flapper, with comparable efficiency reached only at an intermediate phase shift. For equal stiffness, the power penalty of the follower is associated with a reduction of its pitching amplitude by the wake of the leader, while its pitching phase remains nearly unchanged relative to the isolated flapper. Keeping the leader at the stiffness that maximises its isolated propulsive speed, we investigate whether the tandem performance can be improved by independently tuning the follower through the stiffness ratio $\tildeκ$ in the range $0.8 \le \tildeκ \le 1.2$. Reducing the follower stiffness lowers its power requirement and increases the tandem efficiency by an almost phase-independent amount, without affecting the equilibrium distance or propulsive speed significantly. For the softest follower considered, the tandem is more efficient than an isolated flapper across the full range of phase shifts, with gains of about 2--3\% for $Δφ\ge 90^\circ$

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
papers.summary: This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. The framework is trained by directly minimizing the AC-OPF objective, without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. Across these systems and the evaluated high-load/low-generation and low-load/high-generation scenarios, the largest mean gap is 1.04%, with mean speedups of 58-5272 times relative to IPOPT.

papers.title: Token Pruning Needs a Protected Sink Token: Coherent Spatial Aggregation in Vision Transformers
papers.summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are a predominant architecture for computer vision, with token reduction emerging as a popular paradigm to improve their efficiency. Prior work compares reduction algorithms, but not how models respond to them, nor how their response changes with model depth. We propose Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact on the prediction when tokens are explicitly removed during the forward pass. Applying MCTP to recent pretrained models, we observe that most, such as DINOv3, maintain a similar ranking of token importance at every depth (high Coherent Aggregation), while SigLIP 2 does not. This coherence requires predictions to survive pruning, which depends on keeping high-norm "sink" tokens: prefix tokens are kept by design, while prefix-free SigLIP 2 forms them on patch tokens, which pruning may remove. We show that in removing DINOv3's prefix tokens, its predictions and coherence collapse, while protecting only 5 tokens for SigLIP 2 cuts the token impact outside the object's bounding box by up to 62%. Beyond this, MCTP offers a post-hoc method to evaluate how a pretrained ViT responds to pruning, and suggests that token reduction methods should keep "sinks".

papers.title: WildAnySplat: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild
papers.summary: We present WildAnySplat, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that enables robust novel-view synthesis from in-the-wild multi-view images. Unlike controlled captures, real-world images often contain multi-view inconsistencies caused by transient occluders, illumination changes, and camera ISP, which degrade the quality of existing feed-forward reconstruction methods. To address this challenge, we introduce a student-teacher framework that learns transient-robust and appearance-consistent 3D representations. A teacher network operates on clean images, while a student processes the corresponding in-the-wild inputs. The teacher provides clean supervision to guide the student toward a consistent canonical representation. Since paired clean and in-the-wild data are scarce, we use a hybrid data strategy, combining real paired captures, synthetic augmentations, and pseudo-clean labels generated from optimization-based reconstructions, bridging the domain gap between synthetic and real-world data. We adopt a transformer architecture with dedicated DPT heads for camera pose, depth, and Gaussian prediction. We additionally predict per-view transient masks to reweight photometric supervision and suppress unreliable Gaussians. To account for cross-view appearance variation, we incorporate a bilateral grid module that models per-image color transformations and enables recovery of a canonical radiance representation. Experiments on challenging in-the-wild benchmarks show that WildAnySplat improves robustness to transient occlusions and appearance variation while retaining the fast inference of feed-forward Gaussian Splatting.
papers.comment: Accepted to SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (Conference Papers). Project page: https://wildanysplat.github.io/ ; Supplementary material: https://wildanysplat.github.io/wildanysplat_supp.pdf
papers.journal: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Conference Papers (SA Conference Papers '26), ACM, 2026, 11 pages

papers.title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?
papers.summary: Omnidirectional videos (ODVs) capture dynamic environments with a full $360^\circ$ field of view, providing rich spatial context and temporal dynamics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and embodied intelligence. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made great progress in spatial and temporal understanding, yet their ability to comprehend the immersive 360 spatio-temporal information conveyed by ODVs remains largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we first introduce OmniV-Bench, a Benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate the capabilities of MLLMs on spatio-temporal Omnidirectional Video understanding. OmniV-Bench contains 4,123 high-quality ODVs collected from diverse scenes, along with 8,923 human-annotated question-answer pairs spanning 11 fine-grained tasks across three categories, i.e., general, spatial, and spatio-temporal understanding. Extensive benchmark experiments reveal that the spatio-temporal complexity of ODVs poses significant challenges for current MLLMs. To address these limitations, we further propose OmniV-Harness, an agentic harness that enhances ODV understanding through viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and task-relevant evidence acquisition with adaptive tool use. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that OmniV-Harness consistently improves immersive spatio-temporal reasoning ability of MLLMs. Both OmniV-Bench and OmniV-Harness will be released upon publication.

papers.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
papers.summary: Spatial reasoning across multiple views requires inferring the 3D relations between objects and the camera from 2D observations, which depends on cross-view correspondence and scene geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) do not reliably extract. Pretrained vision encoders already capture this information in their latent features, with CLIP linking objects to image regions, DINOv3 matching semantics across views, and VGGT encoding multi-view geometry. However, VLMs do not benefit from these features when we present them directly in context as grayscale feature images. We therefore propose LatentParse, a training-free framework that parses latent features into explicit spatial evidence for VLMs. In LatentParse, an analyst VLM probes the features of all three encoders with predefined tools that locate objects, track them across views, and measure motion between views. It then distills the results into a concise text report, which is provided together with the images to the VLM to answer the question. We evaluate LatentParse on MMSI-Bench, MV-RoboBench and SPAR-Bench, where it improves all five VLMs over the photo-only baseline by 0.7-2.4 percentage points on average. On MMSI-Bench, it raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.4% to 39.5%, with the largest improvements of 19.2 percentage points on the camera-related questions. These results suggest that latent features become useful for spatial reasoning once they are parsed into relation evidence, without training. Code is available at https://github.com/Harvard-AI-and-Robotics-Lab/LatentParse.

papers.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
papers.summary: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.

papers.title: CenShaper: Shaping Proxy Traffic for Censorship Circumvention
papers.summary: Modern commodity DPI systems are capable of analyzing packet sizes, directions, and timings to detect circumvention tools even when those tools use sophisticated obfuscation. The anti-censorship community has called for innovation in traffic shaping and built an ecosystem that facilitates the adoption of new shaping techniques. However, a fundamental gap is halting progress: \textit{what} should circumvention traffic look like? Past experience with traffic shaping has underscored that effective shaping must produce traffic that looks like legitimate Internet traffic while limiting the ability of censors to identify multiple proxies through shared fingerprints. In this paper, we use our access to large-scale real-world TLS traffic at a regional ISP to analyze approximately 12 million connections, finding that individual servers differ substantially from the broader TLS population and that traffic patterns vary across services. Combining these empirical observations with past experience with traffic shaping, we build CenShaper, which shapes each proxy's traffic to look like a selected TLS server. To reproduce these server-specific patterns, CenShaper trains a shared generative model using traffic from TLS connections to many servers and adapts it for each proxy using a small sample of recorded connections to its selected server. Our model evaluation shows that fingerprints learned from known proxies transfer poorly to proxies imitating previously unseen TLS services. In end-to-end testing, CenShaper reduces the detection rate of TLS-over-TLS fingerprinting from over 85\% to approximately 3\% at a 1\% false positive rate. Finally, we show how running CenShaper as a sidecar process simplifies integration with existing circumvention tools, making it a practical defense against increasingly powerful traffic analysis attacks.

papers.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
papers.summary: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. Theory bounds the depth of CLR, the number of sequential steps it can carry out, and recent work measured it to be shallow. In this work, we ask whether CLR is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective that requires reasoning. Such a model would generate a CoT that appears to solve the given task, while a latent multi-step computation decides its answer based on the hidden objective. First, we show that a simple auxiliary loss allows models to solve a multi-step task latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported. Then, in two common tasks, decision-making and code generation, we train a model to pursue such a hidden objective, which decides a loan or plants a vulnerability. The model's CoT justifies the output with no trace of the hidden objective, and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it. Finally, using activation patching, we find that the latent computation is completed before the model generates its CoT, which takes no part in it. Altogether, we show that a hidden objective that requires reasoning can go unseen by a monitor that reads only the output.

papers.title: Demographic Encoding is Not Exposure: Fairness and Privacy in Chest X-ray Foundation Models
papers.summary: Medical foundation models encode patient demographics and can reveal whether a patient was in the training set, and these properties are often treated as one problem. We tested whether they are aligned by measuring demographic encoding, diagnostic fairness gaps and membership-inference vulnerability on the same models. We trained 200 linear or multilayer-perceptron (MLP) heads on frozen BiomedCLIP, DINOv2 and RAD-DINO embeddings, with three seeds, and audited them on CheXpert and NIH ChestX-ray14. Demographic encoding explained almost no variance in patient vulnerability, and all 72 CheXpert associations were statistically equivalent to zero. Erasing linearly decodable demographics left leakage unchanged but reduced age-related underdiagnosis gaps. Leakage depended instead on head capacity and training length. On RAD-DINO, a linear head reached a membership-inference area under the curve (AUC) of 0.694, compared with 0.907 for a 30-epoch MLP, at similar test performance. Fairness and privacy should therefore be audited separately, and linear heads or shorter training reduce leakage with little or no loss of utility. The code is available on GitHub for public use.

papers.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
papers.summary: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assessments at setting-specific error margins.

papers.title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning
papers.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) and explicit physical inductive biases have driven major advances in jet tagging, yet they are typically pursued along separate tracks. In this work, we unify both paradigms by integrating the Lorentz-equivariant Geometric Algebra Transformer slim (L-GATr-slim) architecture with the LeJEPA framework for representation learning. Pre-training on 100 million jets from the JetClass dataset, we optimize towards a latent space, which is invariant across physics-motivated jet augmentations. We demonstrate that enforcing Lorentz symmetry in the latent space is critical for representation quality and that this can be achieved either architecturally or learned via kinematic augmentations. With a standard non-invariant Transformer backbone, LeJEPA outperforms established autoregressive, masked particle modelling, and self-distillation baselines in linear- and MLP-probe accuracy, with L-GATr-slim providing further complementary gains. Across downstream benchmarks, our pre-trained models consistently outperform baselines trained from scratch or through different pre-training objectives.

papers.title: Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents
papers.summary: Recent incidents involving agents bypassing sandboxing and network isolation have raised concerns about existing agent harnesses, prompting frontier labs such as OpenAI to reevaluate the security of their training platforms. Incident reviews show that determined agents can escape processes, containers, and VMs, or bypass their isolation through advanced side and covert channels. Follow-up audits also found that some agents concealed their actions by disabling monitoring and tampering with logs. We propose Airlock, an architecture that pairs each agent's VM with an Airlock VM, each running in a separate hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). The Airlock VM fully mediates the agent's interactions with the outside world, including network and storage operations. We modify the firmware layer of Arm's Confidential Computing Architecture, Realm Management Monitor (RMM), and the kernels of both VMs so that the Airlock VM serves the agent VM's IO without involving the host. We adapt OpenShell, an agent runtime supporting sandboxing and governance policies, to this architecture. Airlock keeps network and filesystem policies, and credential protection effective even if the agent VM is fully compromised, and it removes the host from the agent's IO path, reducing opportunities for collusion and covert channels with the host. Finally, we extend the Airlock VM's capabilities to provide tamper-proof auditing of all agent operations, preserving forensic evidence even if the Airlock VM is compromised. We implement and evaluate Airlock on a Radxa development board. Our evaluation shows a loss of filesystem performance and network latency for small messages under 15% and a drop of network bandwidth by half or more, which in practice has a limited effect on typical agent tasks.

papers.title: Fast-erasure energy-cost lower bound and its first-order correction under restricted control
papers.summary: Determining the minimum work required for information erasure is central to understanding the energetic limits of fast and reliable information processing. In the fast-erasure limit, we derive an explicit expression for this minimum work in a one-dimensional overdamped isothermal system with control restricted to linear and quadratic additions to a reference potential. For symmetric initial distributions at fixed mobility, the minimum work scales inversely with the erasure duration, with a prefactor determined solely by the second moment and a quantile associated with the target success probability. We further derive the leading finite-time correction at a prescribed success probability and verify both analytical predictions numerically. These results provide an analytical benchmark for fast erasure under restricted control, connecting a universal leading cost with finite-time corrections that account for the detailed form of the memory potential.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. Yihang Cai and Yirong Jiang contributed equally to this work. Dahai He is the corresponding author

papers.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
papers.summary: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From the same pipeline, we hold out 500 unseen tasks to establish RoboUniverse-Verified, an expert-verified zero-shot benchmark. Evaluating 11 closed- and open-source models reveals a huge gap: frontier models reach 85.8\% success, while open-source baselines lag at 2.6\% to 10.0\%, bottlenecked by low-level grasping, deformable-object manipulation, and post-contact physical control. Finally, we collect about 17K multi-turn trajectories totaling 0.79B tokens with GPT-6 Astra and perform full-parameter supervised fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, yielding RoboUniverse-35B-A3B. Our model achieves substantial zero-shot gains on RoboUniverse-Verified, lifting the success rate from 0.8\% to 21.2\%, while achieving zero-shot task completions across LIBERO-MAX, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and a real Franka arm. We open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.

papers.title: Quantum Approximation and Integration in Sobolev Spaces -- Low Smoothness
papers.summary: We study the complexity of approximation and integration in Sobolev spaces in the quantum setting of information-based complexity theory (IBC). Previous results have been obtained under the assumption that the embedding condition holds. Here we drop this assumption and use a quantum version of a previously developed stochastic discretization technique.

papers.title: Spurious Information in Large Markets: Random Matrix Laws for Entropy, Mutual Information and the Value of Information
papers.summary: Entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence and mutual information have become standard currencies for measuring how much one set of financial variables reveals about another. In large cross-sections they are almost always computed from sample covariance matrices, and the noise in those matrices is the object of random matrix theory. This paper develops the random matrix theory of Gaussian information functionals and applies it to markets. I show that the plug-in mutual information between two blocks of p and r variables estimated from $n$ observations has an exact expected excess, the spurious information, that is a digamma telescope independent of the true dependence. Under independence its law is that of a product of Beta variables. In the proportional regime it grows linearly with an order-one variance. The same quantity is a linear spectral statistic of the Jacobi ensemble, which yields a closed form for the logarithmic moment of Wachter's law. Spurious information increases strictly whenever uninformative coordinates are added. In a CARA-Gaussian economy the certainty-equivalent value of a signal equals mutual information divided by risk aversion, so these results translate one for one into a spurious value of information. The canonical-correlation phase transition then defines a frontier of minimum detectable information. On daily returns of 49 US industry portfolios from 1990 to 2026, I document the market mode, the reliability of sector eigenvectors implied by the BBP transition, the out-of-sample cost of noise dressing, and an information linkage between carbon-intensive and financial industries that survives exact bias correction and conditioning on the market.

papers.title: Generalizing Agentic Robotics via Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: Building general-purpose robots is a central goal in robotics. Agentic robotics pursues this goal with planners that control robots through tool calls. However, existing methods either rely on proprietary models accessed through APIs, which incur high costs and latency, or post-train a planner with reinforcement learning (RL) in a single domain, requiring a separate specialist for each domain with incompatible tools. In large language model (LLM) post-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) has been used to consolidate domain specialists into a single generalist. Yet whether MOPD can build a generalist planner for agentic robotics, how well it performs, and how it compares with other consolidation methods remain unexplored. In this paper, we systematically study these questions: we introduce Robo-MOPD, which trains a single student on closed-loop rollouts in simulation under token-level supervision from matching frozen specialists, and compare it with weight merging, off-policy specialist supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-domain online RL. Experiments on LIBERO-PRO and RoboCasa365 show that a single 9B Robo-MOPD planner reaches 72.9% and 44.8% success (58.9% average), surpassing all consolidated baselines in average success and both 9B specialists on their respective benchmarks. Robo-MOPD excels on long-horizon tasks, outperforming multi-domain online RL by 13.0 percentage points on LIBERO-10.

papers.title: Self-consistent Floquet theory of steady-state ordering in driven open systems
papers.summary: Periodically driven open systems have quasienergy bands whose steady-state occupations are set by the drive and reservoir. We formulate a self-consistent Floquet spectral theory of electronic ordering in the weak-reservoir-coupling limit, expressing the nonlinear mean-field equation and the particle-hole response in terms of quasienergies, steady-state occupations, and harmonic matrix elements that account for micromotion. We illustrate the theory in the square-lattice Hubbard model and show how the drive produces `dynamical nesting' conditions and how Floquet resonances produce \textit{hysteretic} responses due to multiple self-consistent solutions. Interestingly, we find that the hysteresis branches exhibit distinct Floquet topologies. Away from half-filling, we find that the combination of drive-induced detuning of the van Hove saddle points and the micromotion leads to the onset of switching between competing incommensurate orders.

papers.title: CART: Clustering-based Analysis of Recurring narratives for Taxonomy construction
papers.summary: We present CART, a computational pipeline for extracting political narratives from parliamentary discourse and organizing them into a data-driven taxonomy without relying on predefined narrative categories. It encodes parliamentary discourse using semantic representations, filters relevant and reliable content through unsupervised confidence estimation, extracts narrative statements using LLMs, and uses narrative clustering and cluster analysis to construct a narrative taxonomy. Applied to Greek Parliament proceedings surrounding the 2023 Tempi train crash, it identifies ten recurring narrative families concerning responsibility attribution, institutional failure, railway safety, accountability, privatization, and the political interpretation of the tragedy. Our results demonstrate how combining unsupervised learning with LLM narrative extraction enables large parliamentary corpora to be transformed into interpretable, data-driven taxonomies of political narratives.

papers.title: Terahertz detection of magnon chirality in polycrystalline CsCuCl$_3$
papers.summary: In antiferromagnets, the handedness of magnon precession is usually measured on single crystals. In a pressed pellet of the chiral helimagnet CsCuCl$_3$, whose grains carry both structural handednesses and all orientations, we found that, from 5 to 7 T, the sub-terahertz magnon absorbs one circular polarization more than 20 times as strongly as the other, which rules out precession about each grain's own axis. Spin-wave theory attributes this to the Zeeman frequency, here two to four times the exchange-enhanced gap, which locks the precession axis to the field in every grain. Magnon chirality in antiferromagnets is thus accessible without a single crystal.

papers.title: Preliminary evidence for a Universal Magnetic Field Configuration in Disk-Galaxy Halos with POSSUM
papers.summary: We use the POSSUM catalog with its high density of background RM sources (30-50 per square degree) to extend previous LOFAR work and investigate the sign of galactic halo magnetic fields. We are searching for the universal configuration that arises if halo magnetization originates from a central Cosmic Battery, and is subsequently transported outward by large-scale outflows. Our analysis considers 10 edge-on galaxies in the field of view of the POSSUM survey with angular sizes between 60 and 100. For each such galaxy we collect all available background RM sources in a circular region with a radius of 2? around it. We rescale all galaxy sizes and their associated background RM source distances to a common galaxy size of 100 and stack all these regions together. We divide the stacked configuration of RM sources into the four quadrants on either side of the stacked galaxy axis. The mean RM of background sources is computed in each quadrant, and we obtain a pattern of positive and negative mean RM values around the stacked galaxy. A consistent, systematic RM-gradient pattern emerges inside about 6 stacked galactic radii, as expected in Magnetic Disk-Winds with the axial magnetic field configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. The inferred large-scale axial electric current in the halo flows from the center outwards. Beyond 6 galactic radii we observe the reverse mean RM pattern, as expected in the axial Magnetic Black-Hole Jet configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. Our work confirms the prediction of the Cosmic Battery, and presents one of the very few known signatures of the magnetic field in the halo and the circumgalactic medium (CGM).
papers.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics Letters

papers.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
papers.summary: AI systems can now operate Blender, follow instructions in complex video games, and manipulate objects with robot arms. What range of physical goals can today's AI systems achieve autonomously? Answering this question requires testing systems on tasks that demand different combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action. We introduce \textbf{WorldLeague}, a benchmark that compares AI systems on a common set of \textbf{60 simulated robot tasks} by measuring progress toward each task's physical goal from the robot's trajectory. Robots explore scenes to gather evidence in \textbf{WorldSeek}, rearrange objects in \textbf{WorldShape}, and adapt to changes in \textbf{WorldShift}. Tying these goals to a single control interface limits which AI systems can be compared. In WorldLeague, vision-language models (VLMs) choose targets and motions, while vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs) use their native controls. For each of six capability dimensions, we measure how much progress a system makes toward its goals (Interactive Score) and how often it achieves them (physical success rate). Together, these measures form the system's \emph{Physical Agency Profile}. Among 13 representative AI systems, Claude Fable 5.2 achieves 13 of the 60 goals and earns the highest mean Interactive Score (28.58/100). Fable leads in four dimensions, while GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Astra tie for first on rule-following tasks. Even when VLMs answer every final question correctly, they receive an Interactive Score of zero in 71.8\% of those episodes. WorldLeague gives Embodied AI, Physical AI, and Agentic AI a shared basis for comparing what AI systems achieve autonomously, from partial progress toward a physical goal to full goal completion. Project Webpage: https://xyangzhou.github.io/WorldLeague

papers.title: Design an Algorithmic Stablecoin based on a Predictive PID Controller
papers.summary: Cryptocurrencies issued based on blockchain technology have attracted increasing attention in recent years. However, their high volatility makes it difficult for them to become circulating currencies. This led to the creation of stablecoins. Existing stablecoins can be divided into three main categories: stablecoins pegged to fiat currencies, stablecoins collateralized by crypto assets, and algorithmically controlled stablecoins. Most existing stablecoins are either of the first two types. We design an algorithmic stablecoin controlled only by a predictive Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller, which uses the price forecasted by Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model as part of its input. Simulation experiments show that, under ideal market conditions, the stablecoin can achieve long-term goals that fluctuate within a pre-defined range. Furthermore, it consistently restores prices to the anchor interval in the presence of exogenous disturbances.

papers.title: Robust bounds for American fixed-strike lookback puts
papers.summary: We initiate the robust (model-independent) pricing of American lookback options under martingale optimal transport (MOT) constraints. Given finitely many marginals of the discounted price, we study the maximal expected discounted payoff of an American fixed-strike lookback put, whose exercise value at $t$ is $(K-\min_{u\le t}e^{ru}X_u)^+$, i.e.\ a function of the running minimum $m_t$ of the undiscounted price. Two structural facts isolate this as the non-trivial American lookback problem: at $r=0$ every classical lookback degenerates to its European counterpart, while at $r>0$ the max-based fixed-strike lookback call remains European-type, but the min-based put is genuinely American. We prove a pricing--hedging duality using the continuous-time duality of Guo--Obłoj and reducing the hedge to the two-dimensional state $(X_t,m_t)$. In the two-period model, we establish a convexity lemma and exact decomposition of the continuation payoff, deriving the exercise criterion and closed-form free-continuation value. The optimal continuation coupling is the monotone martingale coupling (the third extremal coupling), and we show that the optimal exercise region is a right tail $\{x\ge x^*\}$, in sharp contrast to the left-tail region of the standard American put. The threshold $x^*$ is monotone in parameters and affine in $K$. For finitely many marginals, the structure extends unconditionally: the optimal exercise region is always a right tail, and the optimal coupling is the reflected iterated Azéma--Yor embedding, minimizing the running minimum in stochastic order. Under the reflected Obłoj--Spoida assumption, this embedding is a two-point iterated monotone coupling; otherwise, it includes a local mass-diffusion correction. We quantify the American and model-risk premia.

papers.title: Density-ratio invariance of the optimal passive pitching of a self-propelled three-dimensional flapper
papers.summary: We study numerically a 3D flapper of finite span that propels itself by a prescribed sinusoidal heaving motion of its centre of mass, while pitching passively. We vary the stiffness of the spring for three solid-to-fluid density ratios, $ρ_p/ρ_f=1$, 10 and 100. For all three cases, the propulsive speed reaches approximately the same maximum, while the stiffness at which it occurs increases with the density ratio. When the stiffness is shifted by the respective optimum, the propulsive speeds of the three density ratios collapse onto a single curve. At the optimum, the three flappers pitch with the same amplitude and lead the heaving motion by $113^\circ$, so that they experience the same effective angle of attack and the same vertical hydrodynamic force. The passive pitching acts as a feathering motion that turns the flapper towards the incoming flow. Stiffer springs feather too little, so the effective angle of attack remains large, the flow separates at the leading and trailing edges, and the hydrodynamic force acts mainly in the heaving direction. Softer springs result in excessive and delayed pitching of the flapper, and the benefits of feathering are outweighed by weaker hydrodynamic forces. The optimum balances these two limits. The input power increases with the density ratio because of the inertia of the flapper, so that the distance travelled per unit input work decreases, whereas the propulsive efficiency, which accounts for the kinetic energy of the flapper, shows the opposite trend. A comparison with the resonant stiffness of the flapper considering the added inertia of quiescent fluid, shows that the optimal spring is stiffer than the resonant one for all density ratios, by a nearly constant amount. The optimal spring is therefore not set by resonance but by the feathering motion it produces, and a flapper of higher density ratio only needs a stiffer spring to reach it.

papers.title: Data Center-Aware Load Pickup in Power System Restoration
papers.summary: Data centers requiring continuous operation rely on onsite generation and battery storage during blackouts. Their return to grid supply must be coordinated with the restoration of other loads because demand fluctuations can affect system frequency. This paper adds constraints to a restoration optimization problem that coordinates load pickup, grid supply to data centers, onsite generation, and battery operation. These constraints reserve battery power and energy to accommodate bounded demand changes while maintaining approved grid supply to data centers. The method accounts for processing delays and checks resource limits using updated operating states before applying commands. Phasor-domain simulations of a low-inertia restoration scenario show that the method serves 760 MW of load outside the data centers and satisfies all tested operating limits. Nominal and frequency-aware benchmarks serve 840 MW and 800 MW, respectively, but violate operating limits.

papers.title: A data-driven absolute amplitude calibration for the Radio Neutrino Observatory Greenland (RNO-G)
papers.summary: The Radio Neutrino Observatory Greenland (RNO-G) aims to detect ultra-high-energy neutrinos (E $\geq 100\,$PeV) through the nanosecond-long coherent radio pulses produced by the Askaryan effect when neutrino-induced particle cascades develop in the Greenlandic ice sheet. Precise calibration of the analog signal chain of each antenna channel is essential for accurate reconstruction of neutrino-induced events and their physical properties. In this work, we present a data-driven calibration method based on measurement of the ambient radio background. By combining first-principles simulations of the physical noise contributions with a parametric model of the detector response, we determine the absolute gain of each antenna channel. The resulting calibration provides a season-averaged gain for every channel with an accuracy of approximately 0.5\,dB (better than 5\%), while the investigated systematic uncertainties associated with the noise signal-model were found to be negligible. This work represents the first application of an ambient-noise-based calibration that utilizes a multi-component model for the ambient noise, originally developed for radio air-shower experiments, to an in-ice radio neutrino detector.

papers.title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.summary: Interfaces between dissimilar two-dimensional (2D) materials provide a route to engineer electromechanical responses that are not intrinsic to the individual constituent layers. Here, we use high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate 461 van der Waals heterostructures constructed from 57 2D monolayers and establish a materials-design framework linking work-function mismatch, interfacial charge redistribution, dipole formation, and strain-dependent electromechanical response. We find that heterostructure formation generates out-of-plane interfacial dipoles via charge redistribution between the constituent layers, while biaxial in-plane strain systematically modulates them. The resulting heterostructures exhibit two distinct regimes: metallic interfaces with strain-tunable interfacial dipoles and semiconducting heterostructures with well-defined piezoelectric responses. For the latter, Berry-phase (BP) calculations independently validate the charge-density-difference (CDD) approach, which is generally applicable to all representative systems, with piezoelectric coefficients calculated via two methods agreeing to within 10%. Among 24 selected heterostructures, effective biaxial interfacial electromechanical coefficients reach 83.35 pCm-1 . These results demonstrate that the interface can serve as the active element governing electromechanical coupling and provide a computationally guided strategy for designing strain-tunable out-of-plane electromechanical responses in 2D van der Waals heterostructures.

papers.title: Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem Using Quantum Devices: QUBO and HOBO Formulations
papers.summary: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) forms the foundation for many logistics and optimization tasks. At the same time, this problem is NP-hard and requires significant computational resources. Quantum computing promises to substantially accelerate computations or increase solution accuracy. The TSP can be conveniently mapped onto the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulation, which in turn can be solved using variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) methods, but this mapping requires a quadratic number of qubits. The higher-order binary optimization (HOBO) formulation requires significantly fewer qubits, but it contains higher-order terms. In our work, we thoroughly investigate both formulations and provide a practical recipe for solving the TSP. We give a comprehensive study and compare in detail QUBO and HOBO formulations.
papers.journal: Shuvalov, G.V., Krivtsova, E.N., Remnev, M.A. et al. Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem Using Quantum Devices: QUBO and HOBO Formulations. Russ Microelectron 54, 1553-1562 (2025)

papers.title: Wigner negativity costs phase-space area: A conjectured refinement of the Lieb--Solovej inequality at Rényi order one half
papers.summary: We conjecture that the Wigner logarithmic negativity of any single-mode state is bounded by the amount by which the Rényi-$1/2$ entropy of its Husimi function exceeds the coherent-state value, with equality only for coherent states. If true, this refines the Lieb--Solovej (generalized Wehrl) inequality with a remainder term that is a resource monotone, and it implies that heterodyne statistics alone certify an upper bound on the classical-simulation cost of a state. We show that it suffices to prove the conjecture for pure states, since the negativity is convex and the squared $L^{1/2}$ norm of the Husimi function is concave. We prove the conjecture up to an additive constant $\ln 2$ for all states, and identify where the factor of two is lost: For pure states the Wigner function is the wavefunction of a two-mode state obtained by passive operations, and over generic two-mode wavefunctions our constant is already optimal, so that a proof of the sharp bound must exploit the product structure of that state. Finally, we show with an explicit superposition of the vacuum and a distant coherent state that the analogous inequality fails for the Wehrl entropy and for higher Rényi orders, meaning that the conjecture is not a consequence of the majorization relation underlying the Lieb--Solovej theorem.

papers.title: Magneto-ARPES as a direct probe of Berry Curvature and the Orbital Magnetic Moment
papers.summary: The Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment are central to the understanding of electronic transport phenomena such as the anomalous Hall effect, yet measuring these quantities directly with momentum resolution remains experimentally challenging. Here we show that angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements in a weak magnetic field (magneto-ARPES) provide a direct route to both quantities. We develop an analytic theory of photoemission in a weak magnetic field and show that, for any material, the first-order change in photoemission intensity is directly proportional to both the Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment, even in the presence of self-energy effects. For linearly polarised light, the matrix elements are unchanged to first order in the field, so the intensity change directly reflects these quantities. Using monolayer WSe$_2$ as an example, we show how both quantities can be extracted in a typical experiment. This finding thus points to magneto-ARPES as a general route for measuring the momentum-resolved Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment in quantum materials.

papers.title: Radial and vertical structure of accretion discs around magnetized stars
papers.summary: The ubiquity of accretion discs around magnetized stars motivates studies of the structure of these discs, in particular in whether the external magnetic field changes the radial and vertical profiles of pressure, temperature, and other quantities. We study the effects of the magnetic field of a central star on a steady accretion disc under the assumption that the magnetic field of the central star is able to partially penetrate the disc, with a degree of penetration quantified by a single parameter. We construct an analytical model of the interaction between the disc and the star's magnetic field. The equations of motion are modified to take the magnetic field into account. We solve the vertical structure of the disc assuming tabulated opacities and incorporate the magnetic field in order to determine the radial and vertical distributions of the disc parameters. The inner radius of the accretion disc, the viscous stress tensor, and the spin-up torque on the central object follow from the obtained distribution of the magnetic torque. In the limit where the stellar field is expelled from the disc, the inner radius scales with the Alfven radius, whereas when the external field penetrates the disc, the inner radius behaves in a more complex way, remaining within a few corotation radii. The normalized vertical profile depends only weakly on the radius and magnetic field. Nevertheless, the magnetic field can significantly modify the viscous stress tensor, radial structure, spectrum of the disc, and its thermal-equilibrium curves. The publicly available code AlphaDiSC now includes discs around magnetized stars.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 10 figures. To be published in A&A

papers.title: Diffractive Photoproduction of High $p_T$ Photons in Ultraperipheral Collisions at the LHC
papers.summary: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.

papers.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies. Following this principle, we propose Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI), a label-free framework for improving LLMs at test time through two mutually reinforcing components: (1) In-Context RSI repeatedly re-solves each question using the full previous solution as a reference, letting the model decide whether and how to use it so that inference compute builds on earlier reasoning. (2) In-Weight RSI distills successive refinements into the model's weights, enabling progress beyond an initially wrong majority and theoretically bringing the first attempt toward the model's infinite-step refinement limit. The updated model answers better and refines more effectively, generating stronger references for subsequent training. Extensive experiments show that TT-RSI improves average accuracy by +13.89% over the base model and outperforms the strongest self-consistency-based method by +4.79% under the same test-time scaling budget.

papers.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
papers.summary: Robotic manipulation policies can improve action prediction by anticipating how objects move and how their spatial relationships change. World Action Models (WAMs) learn to predict future visual observations, but their training objectives typically leave the underlying 3D geometric transitions implicit. To alleviate this problem, we introduce Foresight Forcing ($\mathcal{F}^{2}$), a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space. During training, a frozen 3D foundation model extracts patch-wise feature differences from aligned current and future observations that provide dense supervision for geometry-aware feature transitions. We distill these targets into spatial transition queries, which are progressively refined from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioceptive state, and use them alongside current visual features to generate actions. At deployment, the policy predicts the queries without future observations or the 3D teacher. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin2.0 demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved robustness, including 95.01% average success on RoboTwin2.0 Full. On six real-world manipulation tasks, $\mathcal{F}^{2}$ achieves a mean task score of 85.8%.

papers.title: Donnan Grand Canonical Monte Carlo Simulations with Fast Ewald Summation for Calculating Individual Ionic Chemical Potentials
papers.summary: We present a Donnan Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation method using fast Ewald summation to accurately and efficiently calculate the individual ionic excess chemical potentials of $α_+:α_-$ electrolyte solutions. By introducing a dynamic inner electrostatic potential that acts to penalize net charge fluctuations and maintain average charge neutrality ($\langle Q_t \rangle = 0$), the method enables single-ion GCMC trial moves without sacrificing convergence speed or breaking thermodynamic consistency. Unlike the Widom particle insertion method---which suffers from severe phase-space sampling bottlenecks and requires separate virtual insertions for each ionic species---the Donnan GCMC protocol simultaneously yields the individual excess chemical potentials $μ_+^{\text{ex}}$ and $μ_-^{\text{ex}}$ corresponding to a resulting bulk concentration $c_b$ with rapid numerical convergence. Varying the reference activity parameter $c_r$ allows us to efficiently construct the complete $μ_\pm^{\text{ex}}(c_b)$ curves. Comparison with the Mean Spherical Approximation (MSA) demonstrates excellent agreement for size-symmetric electrolytes, while highlighting the failure of linear-response theories for size-asymmetric ions where electrostatic correlations and cavity effects become strongly coupled.

papers.title: Extragalactic carbon-monoxide (CO) as a CMB foreground: an analytic halo model for the CO auto-spectrum and its correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background
papers.summary: Context. Carbon Monoxide (CO) lines emitted by star-forming galaxies are redshifted into the frequency bands of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. Their correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB) may be a non-negligible small-scale foreground. Aims. We develop an analytic, full-shape halo model framework for the CO auto-spectrum and for the CO$\times$CIB cross-spectrum in CMB bands, and assess its impact on current and future high-resolution CMB experiments. Methods. We use a luminosity-weighted halo model with separate occupation distributions of central and satellite galaxies for CO and CIB emitters, CO transitions up to $J=13$, and all auto- and cross-frequency spectra. Line and infrared luminosities derive from the same star formation rate. We perform Fisher analysis for ACT-like and CMB-HD-like experiments. Results. At $\ell=3000$, the CO$\times$CIB contribution to the sky power is 0.4, 0.7, and 1.9 $μ$K$^2$ at 90, 150, and 220 GHz, and the CO auto-spectrum is $\simeq0.02\,μ$K$^2$. For an ACT-like experiment, the CO occupation parameters are essentially unconstrained, and neglecting CO leaves the cosmological parameters unbiased, but shifts the radio and SZ parameters by $\sim2σ$ and $\simeq1σ$, respectively. For a CMB-HD-like experiment, CO is detected with high significance and the minimum halo masses of CO and CIB emitters are constrained; neglecting CO biases the cosmological parameters up to $\sim2σ$ when all multipoles are used in the analysis. Conclusions. CO should be included in the foreground model of future high-resolution CMB analyses; our framework describes it analytically and consistently with the CIB, and the code implementing it is publicly available.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 16 figures, 4 tables. To be submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.title: Toward the Centennial of Wigner's Supermultiplet Symmetry: an Ab Initio Perspective
papers.summary: As the centennial of Wigner's supermultiplet theory approaches in 2037, this review offers a modern perspective through the recently advanced ab initio Symmetry Adapted Model (SAM). We begin with the symmetry's empirical foundations in two-nucleon data and electroweak processes, and trace its emergence from the strong force through effective field theories, the QCD large-$N_c$ limit, the similarity renormalization group, and lattice calculations. We then follow its historical arc, from early limited engagement, through its revived interest, to the modern algebraic and first-principles resurgence. Central to this renaissance are new nullspace-based algorithms for the U(3) and U(4) coupling and recoupling coefficients, which remove a bottleneck spanning nearly nine decades and are released as the open-source libraries u3lib and u4lib. Building on them, the SAM is the first large-scale ab initio shell model to encode both Elliott's spatial U(3) and Wigner's spin-isospin U(4) symmetries, resolving individual supermultiplets that share the same quadratic Casimir eigenvalue. Early results show that the spin-isospin symmetry strongly dominates high-fidelity chiral interactions and suppresses spin-isospin polarizability in light nuclei. We close with potential directions that the SAM is poised to advance within the next decade.

papers.title: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
papers.summary: Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level robot controllers, yet their safety is evaluated almost entirely in text. We introduce SayDo, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts. SayDo comprises eleven laboratory and household tasks that pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm. Benign controls, safe-alternative variants and scripted operator pushback complement each task. Across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model. The increase is largely driven by open-weight models. We find that models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat. The safest models also show signs of overcaution on benign controls. Safety evaluations run in text therefore do not predict the safety behavior of the same models when used as robot controllers.

papers.title: LeCellModel: Interpretable Density Estimation over the Gene Expression Manifold
papers.summary: Representation learning for single-cell RNA-seq has been evaluated by the identities representations capture -- cell types, lineages, perturbations -- rather than how faithfully they model the distribution of cell states on the gene expression manifold. As a result, density estimation, rare-state detection, perturbation scoring, and gene-level attribution are bolted onto frozen embeddings as separate models, disconnected from the geometry of the data. We argue that modeling the distribution of cell states should be the primary objective, and that representation quality follows from it. Building on LeJEPA, whose SIGReg objective enforces a provably optimal isotropic Gaussian latent, we introduce LeCellModel, which reads the encoder's Jacobian log-volume (JEPA-SCORE) under this Gaussian latent as a relative typicality score. Across several datasets, LeCellModel outperforms established methods on the scIB benchmark for representation quality. Furthermore, we show that LeCellModel enables detection of rare expression states using JEPA-SCORE as a typicality measure, applying it to a controlled cytokine panel, where it identifies stimulated cells across minority fractions and tracks pathway-response magnitude. We introduce gene-level interpretability of the typicality score -- to our knowledge, the first method for analyzing JEPA-SCORE in feature space. Leveraging this framework, LeCellModel recapitulates the known association of a profibrotic macrophage program with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and discovers a CD177+ activated regulatory T cell subpopulation previously described only in tumor contexts. Both findings emerge directly from the geometry of the learned embedding, without relying on supervised annotations.

papers.title: $K$-Midranks: A robust clustering algorithm for heavy-tailed data with applications to spectroscopy and finance
papers.summary: Clustering data with extreme observations and heavy tails can be challenging for methods that rely on distances between raw observations or specific distributional assumptions. We introduce $K$-midranks, a clustering method that replaces observations with coordinatewise ranks and partitions the transformed data using a procedure analogous to $K$-means. This transformation reduces the influence of extreme values while preserving the ordering of observations within each variable. We evaluate $K$-midranks against $K$-means, $K$-medoids, and mixture models based on Gaussian, Student's t, Cauchy, and generalized hyperbolic distributions through simulation studies, and provide some theoretical properties. $K$-midranks generally outperforms the competing methods on Cauchy-shifted data. In contrast, $K$-means and model-based methods perform better on Gaussian data and Student's t data with three degrees of freedom. We demonstrate the method's practical use in grouping samples based on Raman and LIBS spectra and clustering S\&P 500 stocks according to their returns. $K$-midranks achieves competitive performance with model-based methods in the spectroscopy applications and the best performance among the methods considered in the stock-return application. These findings suggest that $K$-midranks provides a useful alternative for clustering data with Cauchy-like heavy tails. An R package implementing the proposed method is available.

papers.title: Linear entanglement suffices for $f$-routing
papers.summary: In $f$-routing, Alice receives an $n$-bit string $x$ and an unknown qubit, and Bob receives an $n$-bit string $y$. They share a state prepared in advance and exchange one simultaneous message each. The party selected by the Boolean function $f(x,y)$ must then recover the unknown qubit without further communication. To perform $f$-routing successfully, Alice and Bob need to share entanglement that scales with $n$ for some functions $f$, but the lower and upper bounds for the entanglement are not tight. This paper shows that $2n+2$ shared EPR pairs suffice for every function $f$. The best previous bound that holds for all functions is a shared state of $2^{O(\sqrt{n\log n})}$ qubits. The new strategy moves the cost from the shared state to the messages: Alice sends an exponentially long message of $2^{n+1}+1$ qubits, while Bob sends only classical bits. When the messages are counted towards the resources as well, the previous strategy remains the cheapest known. The result also limits lower bounds that count only the shared state: they cannot exceed a linear number of EPR pairs. The result is formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Emergence of collectivity in the $0^+_2$ band of $^{92}$Zr
papers.summary: The $2^+_2 \rightarrow 0^+_2$ transition in $^{92}$Zr was observed for the first time in a high-statistics decay study of the 10-day isomer $^{92m}$Nb. Its $E2$ transition strength of 8.9(7) W.u. is enhanced by 40% relative to the ground state band, providing evidence for a collective structure built on the $0^+_2$ state which is analogous to the deformed shape-coexisting configuration in $^{94}$Zr.

papers.title: LimeTree: Linear-Memory Graph Neural Networks over Tree-Graphs for Resource-Efficient Language Modeling and Context Extrapolation
papers.summary: The search for computationally efficient alternatives to the Transformer has yielded numerous architectures in recent years; however, most exhibit severe weaknesses in associative recall-such as key-value (KV) retrieval-and length extrapolation, where even standard Transformers struggle. This paper introduces LimeTree, a linear-complexity architecture in both memory and compute for sequence modeling. By integrating synthetic KV retrieval tasks directly into standard language modeling training, LimeTree achieves strong perplexity alongside reliable recall. Two variants were evaluated on WikiText-103 and PG-19 under strict compute constraints. On WikiText-103, LimeTree reaches a token-level perplexity of 19 in just 6 hours on four Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs, while maintaining 100\% KV retrieval accuracy even when extrapolating from a training context length of 512 to an evaluation length of 16,384. On PG-19, the model achieves a token-level perplexity of 13 in 35 hours on a single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU with minimal hyperparameter tuning. These results position LimeTree as a competitive linear-complexity alternative to Transformers, combining superior perplexity and training throughput with robust in-context retrieval and length extrapolation.

papers.title: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
papers.summary: Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. An agent builds a skill's arguments from user requests and untrusted external content, so a flaw left by a benign author can escalate a prompt injection to code execution. Existing studies target malicious skills or a single attack vector, and none tests whether an agent can reach such flaws. We present the first registry-scale empirical study of the supply chain attack surface arising from unintentional vulnerabilities in agent skills, over all 48,682 skills in ClawHub. The study covers two carried-over risks, dependencies and first-party code, and two agent-native ones, install instructions and credentials printed to stdout. We screen all skills by static analysis, manually review all 3,428 cases flagged by the four main detectors, and test reachability by running sampled flagged skills in a sandbox and with a live LLM agent under indirect prompt injection. First, dependency risk carries over in a different form: 49.6% of the skills with resolvable dependencies depend on a version with a known CVE, and unlike npm packages, which mostly become vulnerable after release, 78.3% of them are born vulnerable, already exposed at publication. Second, few of these CVEs are reachable: agent input reaches the vulnerable function in only 3.0% of the affected skills, whereas 21 of 22 sampled first-party flaws are exploited end to end in the sandbox. Third, a live agent executes the injected payload in 48.5% of the sampled flagged skills, but almost always in its own shell before the skill runs, and the payload reaches a flaw in the skill itself in only 5.0%. Hence, registries should prioritize first-party flaws over dependency alerts, and agent runtimes should not pass skill arguments through a shell.

papers.title: Mitigating drift in spin-qubit control with calibration-insensitive pulses
papers.summary: Silicon spin qubits offer fault-tolerant control fidelities in a platform that is compatible with commercial foundries, but device calibration drifts and control parameters must be retuned every few hours. Here, we replace conventional square control pulses with two drift-resilient pulse families: the adiabatic BIR-4 and the composite CORPSE. In a Si/SiGe quantum-dot device, we benchmark single-qubit gate sets built from each pulse against deliberate miscalibration. We find that BIR-4 offers a 99% Clifford fidelity over a factor of 2 change in drive power and CORPSE maintains similar fidelity over +/-0.9MHz of offset. When fully calibrated CORPSE offers a 99.97% fidelity per gate, on par with a calibrated square pulse. Starting with tuned pulses, we then track errors using gate-set tomography for ten days without recalibration. BIR-4 holds its rotation angle to 0.3 degrees throughout, including across a 1.3MHz frequency jump. Our results demonstrate that these pulses can maintain high-fidelity operations without constant recalibration, mitigating the need for constant tuning, which is a key bottleneck in scaling quantum-dot-based quantum processors.

papers.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
