papers.summary: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, but also from a partial cancellation of errors. In contrast, for optical absorption spectra calculated within a model Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, GCAM systematically outperforms CAM, showing better agreement with the reference spectra obtained with the diagonal RPA screening in both peak positions and relative intensities. Our findings reveal the important role of error cancellation in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.

papers.title: Personalization of a Commercial Powered Knee Prosthesis Under Clinically Realistic Conditions via Reinforcement Learning: A Feasibility Study
papers.summary: Personalization of powered prosthesis control to individual user needs remains a significant challenge. To address this challenge, policy iteration with constraint embedded (PICE), a reinforcement learning (RL) tuning approach, has been developed and validated. This feasibility study investigated whether the developed approach can personalize a commercial powered knee prosthesis under clinically realistic conditions. To reduce the time for personalization, tuning was initialized with a policy learned offline from one non-disabled participant walking on a treadmill and was then applied to three other non-disabled participants walking with the knee through a bypass adapter on a 5-meter walkway. All participants reached the goal within 8-18 tuning steps (1.7-4.2 minutes of walking), reducing the knee-kinematic feature error by 64-90% on average. These results support the feasibility of implementing the RL-based tuning approach in clinically realistic conditions with space and equipment constraints.

papers.title: SpeechSplice: Pronunciation Control in Encoder-Decoder LLM-based TTS by Replacing Encoder Hidden States
papers.summary: Most large language model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) methods offer no explicit function for correcting pronunciation. Consequently, these systems frequently mispronounce many everyday words, such as proper nouns, heteronyms, numerals, and domain-specific terms. While weight-editing or fine-tuning can mitigate this, these solutions risk quality degradation and must operate offline. We propose SpeechSplice, a training-free encoder-output replacement approach for pronunciation control in encoder-decoder LLM-based TTS. SpeechSplice replaces the encoder-output hidden states of a word with those of its intended reading. Cross-architecture and cross-lingual experiments cover ten public TTS systems in 17 model-language conditions. At the hidden state we replace, the intervention moves pronunciation toward the target reading more often when the generator reads the text through cross-attention than when text and speech share one self-attention sequence. In human evaluations, native-language listeners identified speech generated with SpeechSplice as realizing the target reading in 98.6-100.0% of judgments, while a separate study found no significant naturalness difference from unmodified synthesis. By clarifying the conditions under which pronunciation correction succeeds, this study offers an empirical basis for investigating pronunciation control in LLM-based TTS architectures.

papers.title: PRIMEAPE: A Multilingual Benchmark for Fine-Grained Meta-Evaluation of Judge Models
papers.summary: Large language models increasingly serve as judges of other models, shaping benchmark rankings and model development. Yet, a judge whose rationale consistently supports its verdict may still disagree with human preferences. To study this, we introduce PRIMEAPE, a multilingual benchmark for evaluating judge verdicts and rationales. PRIMEAPE provides 2,205 response pairs covering 243 instructions in English, French, Spanish, Urdu, Hindi, Norwegian Bokmål, and Yoruba, with 11k human annotations of preferences and rationales across relevance, naturalness, truthfulness, safety, and overall quality. Our evaluation of twelve open- and closed-weight judges reveals that aggregate performance conceals differences across languages and criteria, while requesting rationales does not consistently improve agreement with human preferences. Judges also favor the first position, longer responses, and responses from related models, with effects that vary across criteria and languages. Crucially, judges can justify verdicts that disagree with human preferences while maintaining consistency between their verdicts and rationales. These findings show that consistency with a judge's own verdict does not establish alignment with human judgment. PRIMEAPE enables assessment of both, providing a foundation for more reliable multilingual judges. We release our benchmark and all annotation materials under the CC BY-NC 4.0 license at github.com/Toloka/primeape.

papers.title: Dirac-like bands and weak-field transverse transport in ABA trilayer graphene
papers.summary: The low-energy electronic structure of ABA trilayer graphene is composed of light and heavy electron branches, which can be altered by an out-of-plane displacement field. Here, we show that, depending on the values of Slonczewski-Weiss-McClure parameters, a displacement field can inflict a band edge inversion, for which we identify the inversion conditions. This inversion is accompanied by a reversal of Berry curvature and giant topological magnetic moments at the band edges. In a weak perpendicular magnetic field, those topological magnetic moments produce valley splitting, giving rise to distinct anomalous transverse electrical and thermoelectric responses. These features offer a potential route to detecting the band inversion and constraining several of the least established tight-binding parameters, such as the on-site energy shift for the dimer pair of carbons $Δ^\prime$ and the next neighbour hopping parameters $γ_2$ and $γ_5$.

papers.title: Big Tree Viewer: A high-performance browser-based phylogenetic tree viewer with agentic AI integration
papers.summary: Phylogenetic trees represent evolutionary history visually, and the ability to display and explore them is a key function in research across biological disciplines. Very large gene and species trees are becoming common with the increasing availability of low cost DNA sequencing, creating performance and informativeness challenges for display software originally designed for phylogenies with a few hundred to a few thousand tips. We discuss these limitations and introduce a browser-based Big Tree Viewer (BTV) highly optimized for fast display and biologically informative exploration of phylogenetic trees containing even a million tips. BTV can automatically map binomial species names to the NCBI or Catalogue of Life taxonomies and display colored ribbons to indicate taxonomic groups for enhanced exploration. Even without taxonomic mapping, BTV automatically labels groups of neighboring tips that share the first word of their names, such as a genus or gene family name, providing readable large-scale landmarks when individual tip labels are too dense to read. BTV supports metadata display, visual customization, tanglegram-like tree comparisons, statistics, figure export, and multiple tree layouts, including a new spiral form to display enormously large trees. BTV is also designed to integrate with common agentic AI tools, allowing agents to display, style, annotate, and inspect trees at the user's request. The BTV web app is freely available at https://BigTreeViewer.net and runs entirely in the user's browser, with no data uploads to any central server. Desktop versions of the BTV app for macOS, Windows, and Linux are also provided for download.

papers.title: CoSel: Cooperation as Selection for End-to-End Driving
papers.summary: Cooperative driving can extend a vehicle's awareness beyond its own sensors, but existing cooperative end-to-end methods inject shared information into the planner and rely on cooperative driving demonstrations to learn how to use it. The moments in which shared information should change a driving decision are rare in such data, providing limited supervision for learning this behavior. We argue that cooperation need not be learned by the planner. Instead, reacting to shared information requires predicting how surrounding agents will move and selecting a response from the candidate trajectories of an ego planner. We introduce CoSel, a cooperation-as-selection framework that leaves the planner and its ego-only input unchanged. A separately trained cooperative predictor uses observations from the ego vehicle, roadside units, and connected automated vehicles to predict surrounding agents and their future motion. CoSel evaluates the planner's candidate trajectories against these predictions, preserves the planner's choice when it remains safe, and selects the closest safe alternative when shared information reveals additional risk. Each safety intervention is traceable to the shared evidence that triggers it. In closed-loop evaluation, CoSel achieves a driving score of 70.7 on V2Xverse, outperforming the best compared cooperative method by 7.5 points, and the highest average driving score of 85.8 on MDrive. Under missing ego detections, the collision count of CoSel increases only from 17 to 19 in 72 scenarios, compared with 19 to 32 for an existing cooperative end-to-end model.

papers.title: Molecular Pawns on a Surface Chessboard: Computational Investigation of Nanographenes with Atomistic Methods
papers.summary: Atomically precise nanographenes combine tunable electronic topology with localized, coherent spin states, making them candidate platforms for molecular quantum technologies. This review examines the multiscale theoretical framework governing these systems: the hierarchy of computational methods for describing magnetic properties, the substrate-molecule interface, on-surface synthetic kinetics, and supramolecular self-assembly. We highlight how density functional theory, automated reaction-path discovery, and spin-aware machine-learned interatomic potentials connect static electronic structure to mesoscale dynamics, and how magnetic exchange, optical excitations, and spin transport can be predicted before synthesis.

papers.title: Demystifying Detectors Guarding Agent Skill Hubs
papers.summary: Agent Skills has gained widespread adoption as an open standard for extending agent capabilities. To facilitate skill sharing, public skill hubs have grown in popularity and increasingly rely on automated security detectors to identify malicious skills at scale. Yet, the effectiveness and limitations of these detectors remain insufficiently understood. To fill this gap, we present the first systematic study of four hub-adopted and two community-provided malicious skill detectors on 1477 agent skills from seven datasets. Our evaluation reveals that even the best-performing hub-adopted detector by overall F1, skill-scanner with Qwen3.6, still misses 4.9% of malicious skills and incorrectly flags 17.8% of benign skills. To understand these failures, we manually analyze detectors' findings and decision-making processes, identifying two recurring failure mechanisms. False positives often arise when detectors flag sensitive operations, such as credential access, without considering whether they serve the skill's legitimate purpose. Conversely, false negatives occur when detectors recognize malicious instructions or behaviors but underestimate their severity or dismiss valid findings during review, ultimately leaving malicious skills unblocked. Guided by this analysis, we refine the prompts of a state-of-the-art detector, skill-vetter, improving its mean F1 score in eight of nine evaluation settings, with gains of up to 22.7 percentage points. These results highlight gaps in existing skill-vetting practices and underscore the need for more robust and context-aware detection mechanisms.

papers.title: Statistical mechanics of noisy collisions in active matter: Dyson-Landau theory
papers.summary: Active systems and other coarse-grained descriptions are often modeled by generalized dynamics, effective equations of motion that are not bound by the constraints of genuinely microscopic physics. In particular, these equations are generally stochastic on the smallest resolved scale. This poses a challenge to first-principles statistical physics, which usually derives emergent noise on larger scales from deterministic interactions. Here, we show how to systematically incorporate microscopic noise into kinetic theory in the limit of weak noise, i.e., high activity. By means of a Dyson expansion of the noisy free propagator, we derive the leading correction to the Landau kinetic equation for weakly interacting systems. We find that the common practice of combining a deterministic collision integral with the diffusive terms of the Fokker--Planck equation is the correct leading order. For dry aligning active matter, however, the corrections are non-analytic in the noise strength, as nearly parallel particles interact for arbitrarily long times. For noise that acts only during interactions, a minimal model of stochastic interactions, noise and collisions do not decouple: the leading corrections are odd in the coupling strength, partly logarithmically enhanced, and amount to an orientation-dependent effective noise strength. Agent-based simulations confirm the predicted dependence on the sign of the coupling. Even in this minimal model, the effect of noise on collisions can thus not be inferred from symmetry alone.

papers.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
papers.summary: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies. We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. A contrastive objective is used to encourage consistent representations of motion across embodiments. The resulting unified latent action space serves directly as the search space for model-predictive control, where sampled latent actions condition particle-based future predictions. Executable robot commands are then recovered from the predicted geometric motion without requiring an embodiment-specific action decoder. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that the learned latent actions exhibit controllable and compositional motion, transfer to unseen robot embodiments, and support zero-shot manipulation with unseen gripper geometries. Following task-agnostic adaptation, our model achieves 90%, 92%, and 60% success on reaching, grasping, and placing, respectively, compared with DexWM's reported 72%, 58%, and 28%. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot real-world manipulation with an unseen dexterous hand, achieving an 86% success rate across 50 trials on five diverse tasks involving pushing, grasping, and lifting everyday objects. These results highlight the potential of geometry-grounded latent actions as a unified, transferable interface for world-model-based robotic manipulation. Project materials, including demonstration videos and source code, are available at https://vinaymohan0409.github.io/DexLatentWorld/.

papers.title: Interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked graphene
papers.summary: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. We find a rich phase diagram shaped by the interplay between the two pseudospin doublets, including mixed flavor orders at charge neutrality and anomalous Hall metals upon doping. In particular, we identify topological states with $σ_{xy} \approx 6e^{2}/h$, consistent with recent experimental observations. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures + Supplemental Material (4 pages, 1 figure)

papers.title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $σ_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $τ_R$ and $α$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(ζ/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

papers.title: Compressibility effects on the flow-induced motions of bluff bodies: common features from transverse and rotary oscillations
papers.summary: Compressibility effects on flow-induced motions of bluff bodies are examined through two-dimensional direct numerical simulations of undamped transverse vortex-induced vibration (TVIV) of a circular cylinder ($Re=150$) and vortex-induced rotary oscillation (VIRO) of an elliptic cylinder of aspect ratio $0.5$ ($Re=200$) for free-stream Mach numbers $0.1\leq M_{\infty}\leq 0.6$. Response characteristics are analyzed across the first desynchronized zone ($DS\text{-}I$), the synchronous (lock-in) branch ($SB$), and the second desynchronized zone ($DS\text{-}II$). While compressibility effects are noted to stabilize the oscillations in $SB$ in terms of reductions in response amplitudes and fluctuating aerodynamic coefficients, as well as the extent and intensity of hysteretic jumps, in contrast, the oscillation amplitudes and aerodynamic coefficients increase with $M_{\infty}$ in $DS\text{-}II$, where the amplitude variation with $M_{\infty}$ is shown to follow the \textit{modified Prandtl-Glauert relationship} for both TVIV and VIRO cases. This indicates the role of the inviscid nature of compressibility in the $DS\text{-}II$ regime in increasing the oscillation response, as opposed to $SB$ where enhanced viscous stabilization with increasing $M_{\infty}$ leads to the moderation of response. Although the simulations are performed at low Reynolds numbers, the identified trends are consistent with fundamental compressibility mechanisms and may therefore persist at higher Reynolds numbers.

papers.title: Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
papers.summary: Antidegradable quantum channels have zero capacity for reliable quantum communication. However, they can nevertheless transmit quantum information with nontrivial fidelity. This raises the question: how well can quantum information be preserved through such channels? In this work, we exactly characterize the optimal asymptotic entanglement fidelity of quantum erasure channels throughout the antidegradable regime. Specifically, we show that it equals $γ+\frac{1-γ}{d}$ for transmission probabilities $0<γ\le \frac{1}{2}$ and logical dimension $d$. We use fractional extendibility to establish an upper bound on the entanglement fidelity achievable by arbitrary error-correcting protocols. Furthermore, we construct a family of permutation-invariant codes that asymptotically saturates this bound.

papers.title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode. We ask whether a navigator can encode each frame only once, at a constant cost per step, and still remember what matters and learn efficiently from its mistakes. We present GlanceNav, a streaming navigator built on a hybrid MLLM. Its Gated DeltaNet layers carry a recurrent state through the whole episode, while its attention layers keep a short window of recent observations and a small bank of keyframes, selected by how much each frame changes the recurrent state. This constant-size memory keeps the cost per step fixed and allows training on whole episodes with the same memory as at inference. Because the entire memory can also be copied in constant time, we further propose Counterfactual Rewind (CoRe), a reinforcement learning stage that rewinds a drifting rollout to its closest approach to the goal, lets an expert correct a few actions, and credits decisions by the resulting change in outcome. Trained only on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE training splits, with 1,000 instructions for reinforcement learning, a 4B GlanceNav reaches success rates of 71.9% and 73.6% on R2R-CE and RxR-CE val-unseen. On R2R-CE, it outperforms the strongest previous single-RGB method trained without external data by 9.1 points, while running at 104 ms per step.

papers.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
papers.summary: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://pawteam-eai.github.io/native-lam/

papers.title: Distillation of a Normalising Flow into a Compact Symbolic Expression for Real-Time Anomaly Detection at the LHC Level-1 Trigger
papers.summary: At the CERN Large Hadron Collider, anomaly detection techniques are becoming popular alternatives to traditional signature-aware new physics searches. For this approach to avoid any bias induced by the real-time event selection applied in the trigger system of ATLAS and CMS, it should be implemented before the first stage of selection, the Level-1 Trigger. This requires deciding to accept or reject each collision within a few microseconds, a latency budget that excludes the most expressive anomaly-detection models. Knowledge distillation has successfully addressed this issue by replacing a complex anomaly-detection model with a lighter student network. This work takes the compression one step further, distilling an anomaly detection model based on a normalising flow into an explicit mathematical formula. Using the SymbolNet symbolic-regression framework with adaptive pruning, the student is a learned functional form based on a chosen subset of the inputs, providing at once feature selection and compression through knowledge distillation. The final expression contains 577 operations and matches the teacher's discrimination on a test dataset, generalising to four benchmark new physics scenarios. Implemented on a Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ VU13P FPGA, the symbolic student has a nine-cycle latency, corresponding to 42.8\,ns at the post-route maximum clock frequency, and uses 0.81\% of the device's LUTs and 0.44\% of its DSP slices.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners
papers.summary: Can foundation models pretrained for generic numerical prediction serve as in-context robot learners? We investigate this question through tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are pretrained to infer input-output relationships from labeled examples in context. We introduce TabAct, which casts visual imitation as numerical prediction: frozen visual features and robot proprioception form the inputs, future action chunks form the targets, and each demonstration time step provides one labeled example that conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control. The predictor receives no robot-specific training or target-task fine-tuning. With one target-task demonstration available to each method, TabAct with TabICLv2 achieves the highest average success among all evaluated methods on both LIBERO and Meta-World, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.9 and 5.8 percentage points, respectively. Additional demonstrations improve control without updating model weights: with five demonstrations, success reaches 94.2% on LIBERO-Object. These results demonstrate that generic numerical pretraining can provide an effective foundation for in-context robot learning.

papers.title: Coherent Recovery of Nested Codes over the Quantum Erasure Channel Using Erasure Decoding and Quantization
papers.summary: Motivated by quantum capacity results, we revisit nested binary linear codes for the quantum erasure channel through a packing-covering viewpoint: the outer code supports erasure reconstruction, while the inner code performs erasure quantization. We turn this perspective into two explicit decoder architectures. Architecture I requires no stabilizer-syndrome measurements and combines a classical peeling decoder and erasure quantizer with corresponding coherent quantum reconstruction and cleanup operations that disentangle the logical state from inaccessible erasure-environment branches. Architecture II goes one step further and implements erasure belief propagation directly through reversible ternary quantum gates, providing quantum state healing that reconstructs erased symbols while leaving unerased code states unperturbed. We establish sufficient conditions for exact recovery of arbitrary logical states, and illustrate both architectures using the Steane code, including explicit scheduling procedures and coherent quantum circuits.

papers.title: Critical step size of stochastic gradient descent for a linear neuron: an exact solution and the role of the input spectrum
papers.summary: We study online stochastic gradient descent for a single linear neuron in a teacher-student setting with Gaussian inputs of arbitrary covariance. The mean-square errors of the $N$ weights obey a closed linear recursion of dimension $N$, which we solve exactly. We prove that the dynamics converges if and only if the step size is below a critical value $λ_c$, given by an explicit scalar equation that involves all the eigenvalues of the input covariance, and we obtain the stationary error of each weight, which diverges at $λ_c$. This condition coincides with the classical mean-square stability condition of the least-mean-squares filter; our derivation is elementary and self-contained. We then show that $λ_c$ is controlled by the effective rank $Ω_1$ of the input covariance rather than by the number of parameters, $1/(Ω_1+2) \leq λ_c < 1/Ω_1$ in rescaled units: the critical step size is inversely proportional to $N$ only for isotropic inputs, whereas it decays more slowly, or saturates, for power-law spectra. Finally, we extend the solution to mini-batches of size $B$: the critical step size grows linearly with $B$ and saturates once $B$ exceeds the effective rank.

papers.title: Unbinned Likelihoods for Probability Densities with Poles
papers.summary: Unbinned likelihood fits to detector-level data become prohibitively expensive when narrow resonances interfere with a nonresonant amplitude. The convolution of the truth-level probability density with the detector resolution must then resolve the resonances, whose widths are much smaller than the resolution. We propose a simple approach that subtracts one simple-pole term per resonance from the probability density. This term captures the resonant contribution in closed form, and the smooth remainder is convolved numerically on a grid whose spacing is set by the resolution alone. The approach applies to multidimensional densities and to densities known only on the real axis. Using two benchmark problems, we quantify the accuracy, computational cost, and statistical impact of the approach. We emphasise that the subtraction is a general approach to the computational problems of unbinned likelihoods in the presence of poles in their probability density and that it is applicable to a wide variety of problems in experimental particle physics.

papers.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
papers.summary: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.

papers.title: Bridging Continuous-Time MAPF and Industrial AGV Fleet Coordination with Lazy Priority-Based Search
papers.summary: Continuous-time multi-agent path finding on roadmaps (MAPF$_R$) offers a principled way to coordinate robot fleets with geometric collision avoidance, yet its deployment on industrial automated guided vehicle (AGV) infrastructures remains challenging, as highly connected and redundant roadmaps amplify both safe-interval reasoning and multi-agent interaction handling. To bridge this gap, we formalize AGV-MAPF$_R$-CTC, a configuration-space variant of MAPF$_R$ with precomputed continuous-time conflicts that enables the reuse of MAPF$_R$ solvers for AGV fleet coordination with minimal changes. We then revisit continuous-time priority-based search (CPBS), identifying the boundary conditions required by its safe interval path planning (SIPP) low-level planner under priority-induced constraints and enabling earlier solution detection. As a central contribution, we analyze the structure of the priority search space, clarifying which agents are affected by each priority refinement and when replanning can be avoided. Building on this analysis, we introduce a novel algorithm, Lazy-CPBS, which materializes high-level nodes lazily: a child's plans are computed only when it is expanded, so siblings that are never expanded cost no low-level search. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks and on industrial AGV roadmaps imported from a proprietary digital-twin simulator show that CPBS-based solvers remain effective well beyond the agent counts reachable by optimal MAPF$_R$ solvers, while Lazy-CPBS substantially reduces CPBS overhead and offers the most consistent robustness/runtime trade-off across industrial layouts.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

papers.title: Semantic-aware Decoding for Diverse Text-to-SQL under Schema Ambiguity
papers.summary: Real-world text-to-SQL systems often face schema ambiguity, where a question can map to multiple plausible schema elements. To support downstream disambiguation, SQL generation systems should include diverse interpretations among their top-k predictions. However, large language models (LLMs) typically favor a single interpretation, producing highly skewed outputs. We propose Semantic-aware Logit Adjustment (SLA), a training-free decoding method that promotes diverse SQL generation by adjusting token logits based on semantic similarity between schema elements. Unlike prior approaches that rely on reasoning-intensive prompting or task-specific fine-tuning, SLA is efficient, model-agnostic, and easy to deploy. Experiments show that SLA consistently improves interpretation coverage over standard decoding and remains competitive with existing diversity-oriented methods at substantially lower inference cost.

papers.title: Joint Flow-Matching Posteriors for Overlapping LISA Galactic Binaries
papers.summary: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe millions of galactic binaries (GBs) at once, thousands of them resolvable, with signals that overlap in frequency. Separating them requires a global fit, a joint inference of all sources, which today takes Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers hours to days on a cluster and is repeated for each new stretch of data. We adapt recent advances in large-scale diffusion models, flow matching with a multimodal transformer, to learn the joint posterior once and then draw from it in a fraction of a second. We evaluate our approach on a realistic simulator, with full instrument response and noise, priors fitted to a simulated Galactic catalogue, and sources sampled anywhere in the entire 0.1 to 16 mHz frequency band. We demonstrate that the approach is scalable to up to 15 653 sources fitted simultaneously, evaluating calibration and coverage w.r.t. the MCMC baseline. The results show that this approach could be realistically scaled to tackle the full global fit problem.

papers.title: Altermagnetism of MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 in a wurtzite-based crystal structure
papers.summary: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method. MnSiN2 exhibits both Wannier-type excitons with N-p to Si-s transition character and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons with hole on N-p and electron on Mn-d orbital character.

papers.title: Radial mean free path bubble size distribution (RMFP-BSD) from the Epoch of Reionization
papers.summary: Among the many statistics used to characterise ionised regions during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), we introduce one which, while closely related to the mean free path bubble size distribution method from Mesinger et al. 2007, is analytically tractable and substantially less dispersive than that method. The radial mean free path (rmfp) method casts six rays along the Cartesian axes in a 3D volume from a random origin to a neutral hydrogen island. This allows us to better quantify the role of overlap during the EoR, identify isolated or interconnected clusters in the simulation, and study the characteristic peak in the ionisation power spectrum, which is important for 21-cm studies of the intergalactic medium. Moreover, we find the method informative about the properties of neutral H I islands during the final phases of the EoR. We also show that applying both methods in tandem can further improve our insight into the morphology of reionization.

papers.title: An Intergalactic medium centred parametrisation of the 21-cm power spectrum from the Epoch of Reionization
papers.summary: The 21-cm signal from the intergalactic medium (IGM) is a key probe of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we present a model of the 21-cm power spectrum centred on the state of the IGM. The framework combines aspects of perturbation and percolation theory to deduce a physically informed parametrisation of the power spectrum. Moreover, it complements classical interpretation methods, centred on modelling the properties of the first ionising sources. We define the IGM parameters driving the shape and amplitude of the 21-cm signal, from the globally averaged volume- and mass-weighted ionisation fractions ($\bar{x}_{HII}$ and $\bar{x}_{HIIm}$), the clustering of sources, through the halo bias ($b_{\mathrm{h}}$), and the characteristic sizes of ionised regions ($R_{i}$) and neutral islands ($R_{n}$). We extend this analysis to model the redshift dependence of the power spectrum, constraining parameters such as the midpoint and duration of reionization. We test the IGM framework on three reionization simulations (C2-Ray, 21cmFAST, and POLAR) with varying cosmologies, astrophysics, and numerical assumptions. The framework constrains the IGM parameter space, recovers the midpoint and duration of the EoR as well as the minimum mass of halos hosting ionising sources $M_{\mathrm{min}}$, and the redshift evolution of the global ionisation fraction, the evolution of ionised and neutral regions (measured with the radial mean free path method by Georgiev et al. (2026b, submitted)). Moreover, the IGM framework lends itself to joint analysis with other EoR probes, such as high-redshift galaxies and quasars and the Cosmic Microwave Background.

papers.title: Early Realignment of Eccentric Planetary Orbits without Orbital Decay
papers.summary: Warm Jupiters are, on average, more closely aligned with their host stars than hot Jupiters, even at high eccentricities. The low projected obliquities of eccentric warm Jupiters on the tidal migration track are difficult to reconcile with high-eccentricity migration (HEM) pathways that excite large misalignments. We examine whether tides acting on the star can realign initially misaligned systems before their orbits circularize. We extend a frequency-dependent tidal model to arbitrary eccentricities and focus on the $(1,0)$ obliquity tide. This component is stationary in the inertial frame, dissipates stellar rotational energy, and can change spin obliquity while leaving the semimajor axis and eccentricity unchanged. Its forcing frequency in the stellar rotating frame coincides with that of the rigid spin-over mode, which is non-dissipative. The strength of dissipation by non-rigid motions at this same frequency remains uncertain. In our models, enhancing the dissipative response by a factor of $10^7$ produces appreciable obliquity damping for Jupiter-mass planets. The stronger damping for more massive planets suggests that an enhancement of $10^6$ may suffice for super-Jupiters. Realignment can outpace circularization if the planet is already on an eccentric warm orbit while the star is still inflated and rapidly rotating during the pre-main sequence (PMS). If alignment occurs then, present-day stellar effective temperature may be a weak predictor of obliquity. In binary-driven HEM runs initialized at the zero-age main sequence, orbital circularization outpaces realignment in systems with sustained eccentricity forcing. The stellar quadrupole scaling suggests substantially stronger suppression of eccentricity excitation for PMS starts. These results cast doubt on binary-driven HEM as the origin of such aligned eccentric warm Jupiters, even when they lie along the tidal migration track.

papers.title: Geneva seven-colour synthetic photometry from Gaia DR3 spectrophotometry
papers.summary: The well-established calibrations of astrophysical parameters derived from classical photometric systems (e.g. those of Johnson, Stromgren-Crawford, and Vilnius) are rarely applied at present. Instead, spectral energy distribution fitting techniques and the very broad Gaia photometric system are typically employed. However, these approaches have proven highly inaccurate for upper main-sequence stars. In this work, the Geneva seven-colour photometric system was synthesised from flux-calibrated low-resolution Gaia spectrophotometry (BP/RP spectra). The available ground-based observations have made it the most homogeneous dataset, offering a number of astrophysical calibrations and applications. The GaiaXPy Tool was used to synthesise the seven filters. The original Geneva U had to be exchanged with the SDSS u because it is found to be significantly blueward of the cut-off of the BP/RP spectra. The ground-based observations were used to correct for offsets and the known temperature dependence of the effective temperature in the ultraviolet region of the BP/RP spectra. The test using well-known effective temperature and metallicity calibrations on the synthetic photometry (with 21 080 stars) demonstrated the high accuracy of this approach. Further checks for possible correlations between the projected rotational velocity and binarity yielded negative results. As a direct application, the metallicity of 630 open clusters (and, thus, the radial Galactic metallicity gradient) was determined. Finally, we compiled a catalogue of 25 881 397 objects. This work demonstrates that alternatives exist to the widely used three-band Gaia photometric system. The Geneva seven-colour approach can help calibrate and analyse astrophysical parameters, especially those of upper main-sequence stars.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables, accepted for Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
papers.summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

papers.title: Quantifying and calibrating precision gain from covariate adjustment in clinical trials with binary endpoints
papers.summary: Covariate adjustment is widely used in randomized clinical trials to improve estimation and inference of treatment effects. For continuous endpoints, the reasoning is straightforward: prognostic baseline covariates explain outcome variability and thereby increase precision. For binary endpoints, however, the situation is more complex because conditional and marginal effects generally differ in nonlinear outcome models such as logistic regression. We develop a theoretical framework for quantifying the maximum attainable first-order precision gain from covariate adjustment when estimating marginal treatment effects for binary endpoints. We derive a closed-form identity showing that precision-gain potential is governed by an estimand- and allocation-specific combination of the treatment-specific risk functions. Building on this identity, we introduce marginal prognostic strength as a population-level measure of prognostic information and characterize when it determines precision-gain potential and when the two quantities decouple. Specifically, substantial prognostic information within both treatment arms need not translate into improved precision for the marginal treatment effect when covariates are predictive on the target effect scale. We further develop a calibration algorithm for methodological simulation studies that preserves prespecified conditional outcome structures and marginal risks while allowing data-generating mechanisms to be calibrated by marginal prognostic strength and evaluated in terms of estimand-specific precision-gain potential. Together, these results provide a theoretical and practical framework for understanding, quantifying, and calibrating potential precision gains from covariate adjustment for binary endpoints.
papers.comment: 17 pages (+ appendix), 1 figure (+ 1 figure in appendix), 2 tables

papers.title: Cleaning correlation matrices with external information: the Maximum Variance estimat
papers.summary: Rotationally invariant estimators clean the eigenvalues of an empirical correlation matrix but keep its noisy eigenvectors. We study an estimator that corrects the eigenvectors by using external information, namely a partition of the assets into groups such as asset classes or regions. The Maximum Variance (MaxVar) estimator restricts the leading eigenvectors to linear combinations of the maximum-variance portfolios of the groups and replaces the rest of the spectrum by a single eigenvalue. It is a factor model with about n parameters instead of n2/2, and it is positive de nite even when the number of observations is smaller than the number of assets n. We apply it to the correlation matrix of 47 futures on stock indices, bonds and currencies, with the three asset classes as groups. In an illustrative Monte Carlo test, in which the reference matrix has the structure assumed by the estimator, the distance to the reference is reduced by one third with respect to the empirical matrix, against less than 10% for the rotationally invariant estimator. The decisive test is the performance of a portfolio on real data: over 1993-2018, the Sharpe ratio of the risk parity portfolio, which involves the inverse of the matrix, is 1.28 with the MaxVar estimator, 1.24 with the rotationally invariant estimator and 1.17 with the empirical matrix, and the advantage increases when the estimation window is shortened.

papers.title: Constructive continuous and sampled-data control of nonstandard singularly perturbed parabolic systems
papers.summary: The existing results on control of singularly perturbed (SP) PDE systems are all qualitative with stability guaranteed for small values of SP parameter $\varepsilon$, whereas control design is confined to stable fast systems. In the present paper we study the finite-dimensional output-feedback boundary stabilization of SP parabolic systems with Neumann actuators and nonlocal sensors acting on both the slow and fast dynamics. This configuration allows us to treat not only unstable fast systems, but even a larger class of nonstandard SP systems (where the fast dynamics with $\varepsilon=0$ cannot be solved with respect to the fast state). We design a finite-dimensional controller based on the slow descriptor PDE system. We consider the continuous-time control and, for the first time, (even for the state-feedback for SP PDEs) its sampled-data implementation. For the latter, we introduce a multi-rate sampled-data framework in which the slow and fast variables can be sampled asynchronously. We consider time-triggered control input sampling and event-triggered output sampling. We prove the avoidance of Zeno behavior and derive LMI conditions for finding upper bounds on the observer dimension, sampling control intervals and $\varepsilon$ that preserve the stability. Our results include a new finite-dimensional controller design for the parabolic-elliptic equation. Numerical simulations demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports
papers.summary: Auditing corporate sustainability reports requires assurance professionals to map a company-specific checklist drawn from roughly 1,700 regulatory requirements onto the relevant passages of lengthy, repeatedly revised draft reports and to judge compliance. We present SARA (Sustainability Reporting Assistant), a human-in-the-loop recommender system delivered as a Microsoft Word add-in that recommends, for each requirement, the passages addressing it and predicts a compliance verdict while keeping the auditor in full control. SARA casts auditing as content-based recommendation over a fixed regulatory taxonomy and makes per-requirement large language model (LLM) matching cheaper, faster, and more accurate through topic-prediction filtering: on expert-annotated reports, it reduces matching cost about sixfold and runtime by 42% versus feeding the full report to the LLM. It is in production use across PwC Germany's sustainability-assurance practice.
papers.comment: Accepted at IEEE BigData 2026 as poster paper. 5 pages, 2 figures, 1 table

papers.title: Interpretable Discovery of Heterogeneous Causal Dose-Response Curves
papers.summary: Discovering subgroups with heterogeneous treatment effects is a central task in causal inference. While methods for heterogeneous effect discovery have proliferated for discrete treatments, their counterparts for continuous treatments remain underdeveloped. In this paper, we introduce a novel, data-adaptive algorithm for discovering interpretable subgroups with heterogeneous causal dose-response curves. This algorithm combines doubly-robust dose-response curve estimation with recursive partitioning, using flexible objective functions to quantify heterogeneity across potential subgroups' dose-response curves. First, we show that the standard doubly-robust pseudo-outcome for continuous treatments cannot serve this purpose. We therefore construct the pseudo-outcome separately for each candidate subgroup, using subgroup-specific g-computation and a subgroup-specific stabilizing density. Finally, we characterize the differences between dose-response curves detected by each objective function. We establish uniform convergence of the splitting criteria and give conditions for recovery of the population greedy tree. We apply it to county-level data on fine particulate matter pollution (PM2.5) and mortality in the contiguous United States over the period 2000-2019. The discovered heterogeneous subgroups vary by education, income, and race. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the R package discoverHTE.

papers.title: Can Multimodal Fusion MakeSense for Embodied Vision in Degraded Sensing?
papers.summary: Embodied vision systems rely on complementary sensors to perceive and act as conditions change. Even models that accept arbitrary sensor subsets can exhibit negative fusion: adding a sensor increases prediction error. We propose MakeSense, a multimodal fusion framework that preserves sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combines information through shared bottleneck tokens. Training pairs full and subset views of the same degraded observations, penalizing higher error with more sensors. Where geometry permits, the distance readout uses range measurements alone, while the rest of the prediction draws on all available inputs. Paired tests across five datasets reveal helpful and harmful sensor additions. MakeSense reduces negative fusion on MM-Fi. With lightweight adapters and per-dataset training, the same design improves UAV localization on MMAUD, cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Real, few-shot pose transfer to RELI11D, and command prediction on Humanoid-Everyday, where a world model trained on the frozen core's outputs forecasts future fused states more accurately than a linear baseline at longer tested horizons. MakeSense supports embodied sensing across human activity, aerial systems, robotics, and autonomous driving.

papers.title: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
papers.summary: We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. The initial temperature curvature generates a longitudinal pressure gradient that alters the rapidity slope, modifies longitudinal expansion work, and produces a distinct cooling history. For the reference parameters, shear viscosity enhances the resulting central temperature difference much more strongly than the prescribed magnetic stress, while the condition for equal central temperatures shifts with proper time and initial shear. At $χ=λ^*=0.03$, the maximum relative difference in central temperature is $0.18\%$ over $0.6$--$6$~fm/$c$, despite a persistent momentum residual in the prescribed flow. Because the velocity mapping also enters the entropy per unit fluid rapidity, the rapidity distribution remains sensitive to the flow evolution even when central temperatures closely agree. Replacing the prescribed field with ideal induction removes direct magnetic work while retaining magnetic pressure and inertia in the longitudinal momentum balance.

papers.title: Data-Driven Nonlinear Observer Design Using the Koopman Generator
papers.summary: This paper deals with the data-driven design of nonlinear continuous-time observers using the Koopman generator. For systems without inputs, an observer is designed that consists of a linear system part with a nonlinear output injection. Therein, the output injection introduces additional degrees of freedom to ensure an invariant dictionary or a small projection error. Subsequently, this observer is extended to systems with inputs. These results form the basis for a data-driven nonlinear observer design using generator extended dynamic mode decomposition. Probabilistic finite-data error bounds are derived for the observer error w.r.t. the data-driven observer error dynamics and for the corresponding steady-state observation error. Examples of nonlinear systems with invariant and non-invariant dictionaries illustrate the effectiveness of the novel data-driven observer design procedure.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, submitted to IEEE Trans. Autom. Control

papers.title: Task-Dependent Linguistic Measures in Aphasia Discourse: A Comparative Analysis of Narrative, Descriptive, and Procedural Speech
papers.summary: Background: Transcript-based measures such as word counts, lexical diversity and disfluency rates are widely used to describe language ability in aphasia. Each measure comes from a specific elicitation task, and studies use different tasks, so values from different tasks may not be comparable. Aims: To test whether discourse tasks change these measures within the same speakers, and whether the measures follow a gradient from Procedural to Descriptive to Narrative discourse. Methods & Procedures: Baseline transcripts from 61 adults with chronic post-stroke aphasia were taken from the Fridriksson-2 corpus in AphasiaBank (POLAR trial, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03416738). Each speaker produced a Procedural (Sandwich), a Descriptive (Broken Window) and a Narrative (Cinderella) sample in one session. A rule-based pipeline extracted 13 measures, 10 of which were common enough to test. Friedman, Page and Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction were used, with a speaker-grouped Random Forest classifier as a supporting check. Outcomes & Results: Total words and number of different words followed the full gradient, but the step from Procedural to Descriptive was small. For most other measures, Narrative stood apart, while Descriptive and Procedural did not differ. Among the 31 speakers with at least 25 words in every task, filler rate, repetition rate and total disfluency density were higher in Narrative than in both other tasks. The classifier reached an accuracy of 0.61 (always guessing the most common task would give 0.41), mainly by recognizing Narrative samples. Conclusions: Discourse tasks are not interchangeable, and expressing disfluencies per word does not remove the task effect. The task should be reported with every measure, and values should be compared only within the same task.

papers.title: Spontaneous Axis-Switching Swirling in Transonic Core-Annular Flow of Highly Differentiated Fluids
papers.summary: Forcing fluids to interact at high speeds creates a multitude of instabilities. Prior studies considered the consequences of these instabilities for core-annular flow (CAF) or atomization systems. However, the existence of spontaneous axis-switching swirling (SASS) modalities in CAF have never been explored. We computationally demonstrate this new behavior for a CAF of steam surrounded by a cold non-Newtonian fuel. Wave pile-up created 3-D fuel surface disturbances which eventually became thin slender lobes with radial modal deformation. Those slender lobes were subject to further instabilities and resulted in oscillatory tangential velocities that were a large fraction of the core steam velocity and orthogonal to the axially flowing base fuel wave. Since these tangential velocities were not externally imposed by atomizer geometry or boundary conditions, it was concluded that they are self-generating. Frequency analysis revealed that SASS tended to operate at the base wave frequency. We additionally explored numerical uncertainty with our previously validated computational tool and found that SASS behavior can be achieved on a coarse, limited mesh at relatively low simulation times.

papers.title: Fast and Consistent Structure Learning in Graphical Models via Approximate Cross-Validation
papers.summary: Structure learning for sparse graphical models in high dimensions requires both computational scalability and selection consistency. Classical criteria such as (Extended) Bayesian Information Criterion can provide consistency, but rely on model-specific likelihoods and complexity calibration. In comparison, cross-validation avoids such analytic calibration and is therefore attractive for graph learning. However, cross-validation is computationally infeasible and theoretically inconsistent in structure learning. This creates a tension between consistency and flexibility in modeling. In this work, we resolve the tension by developing a scalable graph-recovery procedure built on approximate cross-validation. We demonstrate its effectiveness in learning large graphical models both theoretically and empirically, and establish selection consistency under mild signal strength assumptions.

papers.title: Ask Again: Answer-List Instability in Generative Engines
papers.summary: Visibility in generative search engines is measured by which entities appear in responses, and in what order. Ask an engine the same question twice and the answer list can change: a different ordering, or different items altogether. Across 60,000 responses, we find that answers to the same prompt name a different first item 32% of the time, and even two answers with the same items disagree on which comes first. The first position is a measurement target of its own. A "clear leader" emerges after seven or eight runs, which are the budgets recommended for brand and source monitoring, but a "close leader" only about half the time. After 25 runs, a close leader is identified only 60% of the time. Variability between engines is larger than within the same engine. For open-ended prompts, the gap is more than double that for determinate ones. Search queries and cited sites observed leave most of the disagreement unexplained. Visibility measurement should report, for each engine, which items appear and how often each comes first, each with its own quantification of uncertainty.

papers.title: Search for Axion-like Particles using Blazar Observations with the HAWC Observatory
papers.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can mix with photons in astrophysical magnetic fields, modifying the propagation of very-high-energy gamma rays from distant blazars and producing an energy-dependent enhancement of the observed flux relative to the standard expectation from absorption on the extragalactic background light (EBL). We search for this signature through a joint likelihood analysis of seven TeV BL Lac objects at redshifts $z = 0.14-0.60$, combining approximately 3,000 days of HAWC observations with published High Energy Spectroscopic System (H.E.S.S.), Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov Telescopes (MAGIC), and Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System(VERITAS) spectra. We find no statistically significant ALP signal and derive exclusion limits using the $\mathrm{CL}_s$ method. We exclude photon-ALP couplings at the 95% $\mathrm{CL}_s$ level down to $5.5 \times 10^{-12}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a \lesssim 4$ neV and $4.6 \times 10^{-12}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ near $m_a \approx 6-9$ neV. The systematic uncertainty on the excluded parameter-space area is $-36.5\%$ to $+32.6\%$, dominated by the choice of EBL model. Because the survival probability oscillates with the coupling, the excluded region is not simply connected, and we quote at each mass the lowest excluded coupling rather than an upper bound. The combined limit is set almost entirely by the highest-redshift detected source, PG 1553+113.

papers.title: Programmable Broadband Polarization-Preserving Optical Delay Line with Faraday Mirrors
papers.summary: We report a broadband optical delay line programmable for delays up to 1 μs with nanosecond resolution, while preserving an arbitrary and unknown polarization state of the original light. The delay line comprises bidirectional pass in cascaded segments of standard single-mode fibers, along with terminal reflection from Faraday mirrors (FMs) at both ends. Each segment contains either a short path or a long path, selected by an optical switch. The FMs auto-compensate for random polarization fluctuations introduced by the optical fibers, thereby restoring the initial polarization state. Broadband operation of the delay line was assessed by investigating dispersion of both the fiber and the FMs. Surprisingly, we found that the two-pass propagation in the fiber can mitigate dispersive distortion introduced by the FM. Numerical experiments demonstrated that the output polarization state of the delay line has a mean fidelity better than 99% over a range of 50-nm deviation from the central wavelength. Remarkably, the mean fidelity often surpasses that in the absence of the fiber itself.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 10 figures, Journal of Lightwave Technology
papers.journal: S. F. Hegazy, S. S. A. Obayya and B. E. A. Saleh, "Programmable Broadband Polarization-Preserving Optical Delay Line with Faraday Mirrors," in Journal of Lightwave Technology, vol. 42, no. 9, pp. 3346-3353, 2024

papers.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

papers.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
papers.summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

papers.title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
papers.summary: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9\%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor. Scanning tunnelling microscopy and X-ray standing waves have assigned Ga sites on Ge(111), but the dilute Ga site on Ge(001), where the films are grown, has yet to be measured. On Ge(111), Ga in the substrate may supply holes to the correlated Sn adatom lattice, as B supplies holes to the superconducting Sn lattice on Si(111). Whether Ga can supply holes depends on where it sits and whether it has three or four neighbours. On both surfaces, element-specific measurements and calculations comparing adsorption with substitution could settle the remaining site assignments.

papers.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
papers.summary: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.

papers.title: A Fitch-Based Wind Farm Parameterization for CM1: Implementation, Validation, and Impacts on Convection Initiation
papers.summary: We implement a Fitch-based wind farm parameterization in Cloud Model 1 (CM1), representing turbines as elevated momentum sinks and turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) sources within the rotor-swept layer, with optimizations for computational efficiency and parallel execution. Direct comparison with the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model shows close agreement in the magnitude and spatial structure of wind-speed deficits and TKE enhancement. Diurnal simulations also capture the known dependence of boundary layer responses on atmospheric stability, further supporting the consistency of the implementation. Under stable conditions, the wind farm produces coherent spatial patterns in near-surface wind speed and temperature that extend well beyond the farm. In idealized simulations under conditions favorable for convection, large turbines promote convection initiation tens of kilometers downstream, earlier than in the no-farm simulation. Analysis identifies turbulent entrainment of warmer air across the boundary layer top as the dominant source of an elongated downstream warm band, with a smaller contribution from enhanced surface sensible heat flux. Secondary circulations develop across this warm band and provide sustained low-level lifting. A gravity wave generated by the wind farm supplies the initial vertical perturbation, which intensifies as it is advected downstream within an ascending branch of these circulations and develops into a localized deep convective updraft.

papers.title: Fermionic dark linear seesaw with an anomalous Majoron
papers.summary: We propose a minimal fermionic realisation of the $\textit{dark}$ linear seesaw with spontaneous breaking of lepton number. The small lepton-number-violating parameter responsible for linear-seesaw neutrino masses is generated radiatively by a $\textit{dark}$ sector consisting of a singlet and a doublet fermion, together with scalar singlets. The global U(1)$_L$ symmetry is broken to a residual $\mathcal{Z}_2$ under which the $\textit{dark}$ sector is odd. This breaking yields a Majoron $J$ and makes the lightest $\textit{dark}$ particle stable. The charged $\textit{dark}$ fermion acquires its mass solely from U(1)$_L$ breaking and thus induces an anomalous Majoron coupling to photons. Current bounds on this coupling exclude a massless Majoron for TeV-scale U(1)$_L$ breaking. We add a linear term that breaks lepton number softly and gives the Majoron a GeV-scale mass. Such a Majoron decays into two photons and can be probed at beam-dump experiments. We study the dark matter phenomenology, focusing on the case where the stable particle is a fermionic weakly interacting massive particle. We analyse how the framework can be tested through charged-lepton flavour-violating decays such as $μ\to eγ$, which receive contributions from both the $\textit{dark}$ and the seesaw sectors. Moreover, both sectors enhance the Majoron couplings to charged leptons, so that the Majoron-emitting decays $τ\to \ell J$ ($\ell = e,μ$) typically exceed $τ\to \ellγ$ by orders of magnitude and can probe parameter space beyond the reach of $μ\to eγ$.

papers.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
papers.summary: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches. We discuss several key aspects of their tripartite entanglement dynamics through the lens of the Markov gap. We confront our results with exact lattice numerics and find perfect agreement in the hydrodynamic regime.

papers.title: Pulse-to-pulse Power Fluctuations in Ultra-Fast Fiber Amplifiers with Gain-Managed Nonlinearity
papers.summary: We present a theoretical framework for predicting pulse-to-pulse power fluctuations caused by pump and seed power noise and by amplified spontaneous emission in ultrafast fiber amplifiers operating in the gain-managed nonlinear regime. The numerical model evaluates statistically averaged quantities directly, without Monte Carlo simulations with stochastic sources, and reduces to a semi-analytical monochromatic model in the limit of vanishing signal bandwidth and negligible ASE. We show that nonlinear spectral broadening of the signal and of its perturbations, combined with the frequency-dependent gain, significantly alters the technical relative intensity noise in both the high-power, high-repetition-rate and the low-power, low-repetition-rate regimes, and that in the latter regime the contributions related to amplified spontaneous emission become comparable to those induced by pump and seed fluctuations.

papers.title: How Systems Treat Intent: A Faceted Taxonomy of Intent for Human-AI Co-Creation
papers.summary: Human-AI interaction depends on systems acting on user intent rather than explicit procedures, even when that intent is incomplete, evolving, or partially communicable. Literature organizing systems by interaction technique, workflow stage, or division of labor, offer limited insight into which facet of intent an interaction mechanism addresses. We introduce a six-facet taxonomy of intent, grounded in philosophical accounts of mind, action, and meaning, and apply it to systems presented in 198 papers from eleven SIGCHI venues. Our analysis reveals that different forms of incomplete intent are associated with distinct interaction and authorship strategies, showing that mechanisms that appear similar often address fundamentally different intent-related problems. This exposes blind spots, as intent is rarely represented as an interaction object, authorship provenance is rarely tracked, and tentative preferences are rarely distinguished from firm commitments. The taxonomy offers a lens for analyzing and designing AI systems around the facets of intent they address.

papers.title: Quantum resources constrain function approximation
papers.summary: Universal function approximation is central to machine learning. Quantum learning models are universal as well, but this does not specify the resources needed to approximate a given function. We study how coherence, imaginarity, entanglement and magic constrain function approximation for a fixed encoding and readout, using the cumulative resource power of the trainable gates.
