In a one-qubit model with phase encoding, coherence bounds the oscillation of the model function, while imaginarity bounds its odd part. In a two-qubit model, entanglement bounds the distance from product functions. These bounds hold at any encoding depth. For magic, the phase encoding itself supplies non-Clifford operations. On domains bounded away from zero, Clifford trainable gates suffice for uniform approximation. Replacing unrestricted trainable gates by Clifford gates increases the encoding depth at most polynomially in the original depth, the inverse error and the inverse distance of the domain from zero. Magic in the trainable gates can nevertheless improve accuracy at fixed depth. These results show how the resources of a quantum model must match the structure of the target function.

papers.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
papers.summary: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. The collective predictive coding model approximates this prior by representing the dependence through that shared index. An established Metropolis-Hastings naming game lets agents infer and exchange words using private evidence. Toy and multiview image experiments illustrate how word exchange can coordinate private categories and improve the fit of collective models. The account connects joint attention to shared symbols through the coupling of private inference.

papers.title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors
papers.summary: Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. This condition consists of pointwise inequalities that can be checked for the computed iterate, without establishing convergence of the iteration, and is a first step towards sample-based certification. We further establish inherent robustness of the controller with respect to model errors and recover classical results for the linear-quadratic regulator. Numerical studies on a linear-quadratic problem and on a nonlinear system with known optimal value function are consistent with the guarantees and show that the suboptimality bound is conservative.

papers.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

papers.title: Perfect Spin-to-Charge Signal Conversion via Inverse Spin Hall Effect in a Superconductor
papers.summary: Spin-to-charge conversion is central to spintronics, but conventional spin Hall mechanisms are intrinsically limited by the small spin Hall angle. Here we show that superconductivity can overcome this limitation and enable near-unity spin-to-charge signal conversion. We consider a nonlocal spin-valve geometry in which a spin accumulation is injected into a superconductor and converted into a transverse charge signal through the inverse spin Hall effect. In the superconducting state, the strongly suppressed quasiparticle conductance below the gap allows the resulting charge imbalance to generate a voltage comparable to the injected spin bias, despite a small spin Hall angle. We derive the full nonequilibrium response including finite spectral broadening and finite temperature, and propose temperature and spin-bias-dependent measurements of the detector voltage to test our predictions.

papers.title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
papers.summary: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.

papers.title: What Quality Engineers Need to Know About Generative AI: Structured Data Extraction
papers.summary: In this expository paper, we explain how quality engineers can use large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for structured data extraction. We introduce the relevant concepts, discuss structured extraction from a measurement-system perspective, and demonstrate its implementation in R and Python. We then present two freely available web-based applications (apps): (a) extracting information from automotive recall notices and (b) monitoring quality engineering research on arXiv. To ensure the accuracy of our AI-driven structured extraction, human evaluators validated the results. In the first app, four reviewers assessed information extracted from 30 recall notices using two models, with 98.6% of the 720 field-level ratings judged fully correct. In the second app, 21 authors evaluated information extracted from 45 of their arXiv papers. All paper summaries were rated mostly correct or correct, although the evaluations identified problems with some classification fields and mathematical expressions. These results demonstrate the practical potential of structured data extraction while emphasizing the need to validate the extracted information. We make both apps and their source code publicly available so that readers can adapt the approach to their own applications.

papers.title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs
papers.summary: Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples. The framework is designed with three key objectives: (i) reducing manual annotation by harnessing prompt-based zero-shot and few-shot capabilities of modern LLMs, (ii) flexibly parsing diverse document formats (i.e., HTML, PDF, TXT, and JSON), and (iii) improving accessibility for non-expert users by automatically inducing schemas from document collections, which can then be refined for extraction. We evaluate Trallie with open-weight LLMs on FDA 510(k) documents and on movie and university websites from SWDE. It outperforms previously reported systems when the target attributes are provided for text extraction and is competitive when it must discover attributes for the schema automatically. The project is available at https://github.com/PiSchool/trallie

papers.title: Janus Asymmetry Unlocks Rashba Spintronics and Chiral Phononics in Two-Dimensional Carbo-Chalcogenides
papers.summary: Spintronics and chiral phononics offer complementary routes for nanoscale control, yet realizing both functionalities within a common two-dimensional platform remains challenging. Here, using extensive first-principles calculations, we show that Janus asymmetry simultaneously drives both effects in transition-metal carbo-chalcogenides (JTMCCs) along two chemically distinct routes, through either chalcogen or transition-metal substitution. Remarkably, both Janus routes yield giant Rashba responses, with $α_\mathrm{R}\approx2$ eV Å in Ta$_2$CSSe and NbTaCS$_2$, exceeding those reported for Mo/W-based Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides. Furthermore, Janus asymmetry lifts the degeneracy of opposite-chirality phonons, producing splittings as large as $\approx28$ cm$^{-1}$. More strikingly, asymmetry generates chiral carbon vibrations that were achiral in the centrosymmetric parent compounds, with splittings reaching $\approx8$ cm$^{-1}$. Finally, we show external electric fields tunability over Rashba strength and chiral-phonon splittings, providing a common control knob for electronic spin and lattice angular momentum. Our work offers a unified strategy for realizing spintronic and chiral phononic in two-dimensional materials.
papers.comment: First version of the manuscript (before revisions)

papers.title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts. First, a selection policy picks the one object the robot works on next. Second, a warping policy reads a local view of the scene around that object, whose size does not depend on N. It emits a multiplier and an offset for every quantity the skill reads and every action it outputs. Third, the skill acts under this affine warp. It is shown a scene that holds a single object, while the warp steers it around the objects it is not shown and edits the actions that are sent to the robot. Both the selection and warping policies are trained with PPO on the multi-object reward and use the skill as a black box, so WAVE is task-general and skill-agnostic. It requires only that the skill was trained on the same embodiment and that every object has a goal pose. We also bound the number of attempts needed to place all N objects, assuming positive expected net progress per attempt, and measure this progress for each object count. We evaluate WAVE on cube arrangement tasks with a gantry robot and with a Franka Panda arm. Trained with at most nine cubes, it generalizes zero-shot to several times its training count, on the gantry to scenes of up to thirty cubes. Published methods that learn multi-object manipulation show count generalization up to six objects. Fine-tuning the skill, learning from the same local view without it, and an entity transformer, even when distilled from the pretrained skill, all collapse within their training counts under the same training budget.
papers.comment: 37 pages, 15 figures, 15 tables. Submitted to International Conference on Learning Representations 2027. Code, videos and full results are available at https://hhi-robot-learning.github.io/wave-website/

papers.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
papers.summary: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.

papers.title: Conservative tidal effects to third post-Minkowskian order in scalar-tensor theories
papers.summary: Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order. We retain the full velocity dependence at linear order in the tidal response coefficients. The calculation covers the scalar dipole and quadrupole and the electric, magnetic, and mixed quadrupoles and octupoles. Among them, the scalar dipole enters the dynamics already at third post-Newtonian (3PN) order, two orders before the gravitational quadrupole. At 3PM, the tidal correction to the angle also depends on the first scalar derivatives of the responses and contains terms linear in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. The results reproduce the general-relativistic tidal angle and the post-Newtonian tidal dynamics through 5PN, and a test-body calculation confirms their leading order in the mass ratio, including the Gauss-Bonnet terms for a companion with vanishing sensitivity.

papers.title: On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients
papers.summary: We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete antiderivatives respectively for intricate hypergeometric sequences that arise in our analysis.

papers.title: Geometry-controlled clogging and transport mechanisms in confined Y-junctions
papers.summary: We investigate transport and clogging of hard particles in a confined symmetric Y-junction using off-lattice Monte Carlo simulations. The geometry is controlled by the channel width w and a truncation parameter s that modifies the inner vertex. The flow probability exhibits a sharp sigmoidal crossover, defining a characteristic width wc that depends non-monotonically on s. This non-monotonic behavior persists under variations of the transverse Monte Carlo step, although the absolute values of wc change. Microscopic analysis reveals two distinct blocking mechanisms: single-particle obstruction at small truncations and collective arch-like structures at larger truncations. Residence-time statistics and particle-order inversions provide additional evidence of this change in transport dynamics. Our results demonstrate that local modifications of junction geometry can strongly affect clogging and particle transport, even in a minimal model with excluded-volume interactions only.

papers.title: Identification of Poisson processes through a one-dimensional projection
papers.summary: We study the identification of stationary Poisson processes in Euclidean space through a single one-dimensional projection. Given a point process and a straight line, each point is retained independently with a probability given by a Gaussian function of its distance to the line; the retained points are projected onto the line. If the process is Poisson, the projection is again Poisson. What a single projection reveals depends on the sign of the second factorial cumulant, which is also the sign of the two-point correlations. Under a Palm domination condition, which holds for positively associated processes, the cumulant is nonnegative. Using a Chen-Stein argument we show that when the cumulant of the projection vanishes, the process is Poisson. Consequently, a single projection identifies non-Poissonianity. The same result holds under negative association. When the cumulant changes sign, a random projection detects a nonzero cumulant with probability one. We propose a test whose rejection region is computed by Monte Carlo. The test, together with a spacings-based variant for repulsive alternatives, rejects determinantal, shot-noise and other classical processes. When applied to lunar impact craters, the test rejects the Poisson hypothesis for craters with diameter below 30 km and does not reject it for craters above 45 km.

papers.title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
papers.summary: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $γ_{\rm v}N\toΦ_1Φ_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $γp\toπ^0π^0p$ and $γp\toπ^+π^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.

papers.title: Symmetry breaking Poincar{é}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
papers.summary: We construct Poincar{é}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{ö}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$π$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{ö}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{ö}hm's sequence with a gap to the next one tending to infinity; and large anti-de Sitter black holes in dimension nine with an Einstein horizon have no static $L^2$ perturbation of scalar type, which we prove with an explicit positive supersolution of the Kodama-Ishibashi master equation.

papers.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
papers.summary: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries. Our results are supported by alternative methods, including the TraSPI method.

papers.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
papers.summary: The tools users approve for their AI agents keep changing their JSON input schemas. Of 8 surveyed MCP clients and scanners, none is observed or documented to re-approve a tool whose input schema widens (two not determinable). We define non-amplification over the coordinates visible in the schema (declared arguments and undeclared fields, on effective values) and a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion, trusting no field labels by default and conservative up to its checker and tested case analysis. Evidence: a Coq proof of composition; 48 regression tests; an exact-reference benchmark, where the reviewed version of the rule silently re-bound 27 amplifying changes, now fixed; and a pilot on 604 releases of 39 public MCP servers. There, 412 of 580 compatible schema changes widen some coordinate, yet compatibility re-binds them silently. The authors' adjudicated double annotation finds at least 76 that add or widen an authority-bearing argument (66 of the 84 a name-based labeller flags, plus 10 it misses). On existing tools, the rule asks 645 re-approvals, against 1,197 for pinning the input schema (2,004 with descriptions) and 617 for compatibility. Behaviour change behind an identical schema remains out of reach.

papers.title: Dephasing-Powered Autonomous Quantum Engine with Time-Crystalline Work Cycles
papers.summary: Autonomous quantum engines seek to convert energy supplied by environments into useful work, yet dephasing is usually regarded as detrimental noise. Here we show that local dephasing can instead power a quantum engine: by disrupting ferromagnetic correlations in an interacting spin-$1/2$ ensemble, it injects energy that can be transferred through an LC resonator to a passive load. Remarkably, without any external periodic driving, the coupled system can self-organize into a time-crystalline work cycle that delivers sustained, reproducible power. Within homogeneous mean-field dynamics, we identify two distinct routes to such operation. At weak spin--resonator coupling, the dissipative time crystal of the unloaded working medium survives loading and drives the receiver. At stronger coupling, resonator backaction can disrupt cyclic operation, whereas appropriate load damping restores a stable, self-consistent periodic cycle of the composite system. Finite-size spin-diffusion simulations further reveal rapidly increasing uninterrupted operating times with different size dependences in the two regimes. Our results demonstrate how an autonomous quantum engine can self-organize its collective dynamics through interactions and load feedback to harness environmental noise for sustained cyclic work output.

papers.title: Efficient Shot Allocation and Spectral Reconstruction for Real-Time Quantum Krylov Diagonalization
papers.summary: We develop analytical and statistical methods to improve the energy estimate from the real-time quantum Krylov diagonalization under a fixed measurement budget. We first express the leading energy variance as a function of the number of shots assigned to each circuit setting, accounting for both the sensitivity of the energy to the measured moments and the correlations among outcomes recorded in the same shot.We use an initial batch of measurements to choose how to allocate the remaining shots. Under fixed-model regularity assumptions, the resulting generalized least-squares energy estimator attains the minimum leading mean-square error (MSE) coefficient within the prescribed allocation class, with the initial measurements included in the total shot budget. Furthermore, we use the same data to reconstruct the Hamiltonian and overlap moments jointly by fitting them to a common nonnegative spectral measure. For asymptotically Gaussian moment errors, we characterize precisely when this reconstruction lowers the leading energy MSE in the case where two linearly independent inequalities describe the feasible moment perturbations to first order. Numerical experiments on spin and Hubbard models show that learned allocation can improve Ritz energy estimates at fixed total shot cost. The experiments also illustrate that enforcing spectral consistency can further reduce the energy estimation error.

papers.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
papers.summary: LLM agents turn a user's request and retrieved content into tool calls, and a call can reach the wrong recipient, endpoint, file or participant. Argument-level provenance blocks such values when they come from untrusted content, but accepts a trusted value that the user never requested. IntentFlow, a mediation layer between an unmodified planner and its tools, checks each authority-bearing argument against an intent contract and a provenance policy. On a synthetic benchmark of 200 attacks (oracle intent and injection labels, declared roles), attack success falls from 50.5% with provenance alone to 12.0% [8.2-17.2%]; every remaining success alters a content or payload field. IntentFlow wrongly blocks none of 200 paired benign tasks and 4 of 50 hard ones. On 50 trusted-but-unauthorized attacks, provenance-only mediation executes all 50 and IntentFlow none; a CaMeL-style check also blocks all 50 but rejects 16 of 50 benign tasks. On an offline AgentDojo-derived replay, IntentFlow blocks all 20 attacks at 75% benign success, as does a CaMeL-style check; a Progent-style allowlist blocks 19 and keeps all benign tasks. With one live planner and the same oracles, the mediator blocked all 17 corrupted calls proposed in 110 attacks.

papers.title: Geometric properties of concatenated geometric and holonomic quantum gates
papers.summary: We investigate the geometric properties of concatenated quantum gates, focusing on the distinction between geometric and holonomic quantum computation. We show that, although individual gates may be purely geometric, their concatenation does not generally preserve this property, since the cyclic states of the composite operation can accumulate nontrivial dynamical phases over the course of the concatenated evolution. In contrast, we demonstrate that concatenations of arbitrary single-qubit holonomic gates remain holonomic, provided that the parallel-transport condition holds throughout the evolution and the computational subspace undergoes cyclic evolution. The preservation of geometric or holonomic character under concatenation is an important prerequisite for extending arguments underlying geometric protection from individual gates to complete quantum circuits.

papers.title: Comparison of 3D-DXA Measurements with QCT Software Solutions for Proximal Femur Bone Density Assessment
papers.summary: 3D-Shaper reconstructs proximal femur shape and density in 3D from a standard hip dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scan. In men and women aged 35-91 years, we compared 3D-Shaper integral volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), trabecular vBMD, and cortical surface BMD (sBMD) with quantitative computed tomography (QCT) processed with three methods: an in-house pipeline, Stradview and QCTPro CTXA, which were used to derive bone measurements equivalent to those of 3D-Shaper. Agreement, including among QCT methods, was assessed with linear regression and Bland-Altman analysis (bias and limits of agreement, LoA). 3D-Shaper agreed strongly with the in-house pipeline and Stradview for integral vBMD (R=0.95-0.96; bias 1.5 to 4.2 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$39.7 to 41.4 mg/cm$^3$), trabecular vBMD (R=0.92-0.94; bias -11.8 to -7.8 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$33.3 to 39.4 mg/cm$^3$) and cortical sBMD (R=0.94; bias 5.6 to 38.2 mg/cm$^2$; LoA $\pm$23.6 to 26.4 mg/cm$^2$). The in-house pipeline and Stradview agreed for integral vBMD (R=1.00; bias -2.7 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$3.7 mg/cm$^3$), trabecular vBMD (R=0.96-1.00; bias -0.2 to 3.9 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$6.9 to 27.5 mg/cm$^3$) and cortical sBMD (R=0.98; bias 32.7 mg/cm$^2$; LoA $\pm$14.6 mg/cm$^2$). Compared with 3D-Shaper, QCTPro CTXA integral vBMD was systematically lower (R=0.90; bias -28.4 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$61.5 mg/cm$^3$) and trabecular vBMD showed a proportional bias (R=0.89; bias -44.1 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$61.3 mg/cm$^3$). The same pattern was observed against the other QCT methods, for integral vBMD (R=0.93; bias -32.6 to -29.9 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$49.6 to 50.0 mg/cm$^3$) and trabecular vBMD (R=0.94-0.96; bias -36.3 to -32.5 mg/cm$^3$; LoA $\pm$51.2 to 54.9 mg/cm$^3$). These findings support the agreement of 3D-Shaper with independent QCT approaches and show that 3D-Shaper-QCT differences must be interpreted in light of the QCT method used.

papers.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are often ranked by an LLM judge whose error rates are measured once and reused for every agent. The corrected success rates can then be biased when the judge's errors depend on the trajectory and agents differ in the trajectories they produce for successes or failures. We derive the exact asymptotic bias and give a chain of checks from identification to simultaneous ranks. On a four-agent semi-synthetic benchmark, a scalar correction with oracle calibration has maximum bias 0.245 and mean pointwise coverage 0.016, and never recovers the full ranking (0/250 replications). Augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with a uniform or a design-aware random audit keeps the maximum bias below 0.003, with mean pointwise coverage of 0.939 and 0.950. In a 48-cell stress test, effective target support rises only from 0.209 to 0.805 as calibration grows from 600 to 4,800 labels, while audited AIPW keeps a mean absolute error of 0.018-0.020. Without calibration support, or with judge dependence within an externally justified bound, we report valid bounds or sensitivity sets and carry them into rank sets. An e-process confidence sequence stays valid, for a stable target, under predictable adaptive auditing and arbitrary stopping.

papers.title: Place-Revisit Consistency Evaluation of Reference Poses
papers.summary: Reference trajectories are widely used to evaluate odometry and simultaneous localization and mapping systems. However, local inconsistencies in benchmark reference poses can bias such evaluations. This paper presents a place-revisit consistency evaluation method for reference poses in mobile sensing datasets. When a platform revisits a previously observed place after a sufficient temporal gap, the relative pose implied by the reference trajectory should agree with relative poses estimated directly from onboard sensors. We instantiate this idea with lidar scan registration and stereo-image pose estimation, and apply it to the KITTI Odometry and SNAIL Radar. The KITTI analysis identifies several revisit regions where the public reference poses disagree with sensor-derived relative poses, with median translation discrepancies up to 6.60 m. Representative point-cloud overlays further localize these discrepancies and support the use of place revisits as a benchmark-validation tool.

papers.title: Optimizing Locally Equivalent Graph States in Quantum Computing Using Greedy Best-First Search
papers.summary: In measurement-based quantum computation and quantum repeater networks, graph-structured quantum states called graph states play a central role as an essential resource. In a graph state, each vertex corresponds to a qubit, and each edge is prepared by applying one controlled-Z (CZ) gate. Local complementation, which toggles adjacencies among the neighbors of a selected vertex, produces operationally equivalent graph states up to an inexpensive operation called local Clifford gates. Therefore, finding equivalent graphs up to local complementation with fewer edges and lower maximum degree can reduce the preparation cost, such as the number of CZ gates and the circuit depth. In this paper, we formulate the problem of finding a desirable equivalent graph via local complementations as a state space search problem. We apply a heuristic search algorithm, greedy best-first search (GBFS), to the formulated problem. Our experimental evaluation shows that despite its simplicity, GBFS outperforms existing approaches based on integer linear programming or local search across multiple graph classes, including random graphs, bounded-degree graphs, and most of the graphs constructed from quantum LDPC codes. In addition, we empirically analyze GBFS's search behavior, confirming that we need search rather than stopping at the first local minimum to find the best solution.

papers.title: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives
papers.summary: Proprietary news archives assign stories to firms, so reproducing a financial study often requires access to both the articles and the vendor's assignments. CCFinance lets researchers reconstruct firm coverage under different selection rules by recording which version of a story was captured, which issuers it names and how often each appears. From 14.8 million English-language records in Fine News, derived from public Common Crawl News, we identify 5.22 million distinct, consistently dated articles with issuer links. Exact reconstruction requires the restricted snapshot and derived artifacts. We compare GLiNER and Stanza on 250 model-labeled article leads and assess issuer links and story focus against blinded model judgments. Estimated precision among 475 accepted links is 96.8%. Among held-out articles with a detected company, requiring three mentions raises subject precision from 31.9% to 66.1%. Across the 2017-2025 panel, the same rule reduces the number of issuer-years with at least 50 qualifying stories from 13,918 to 8,641. Three reimplementations examine volatility tracking, bank networks and overnight returns. In the network study, bank pairs appearing together rose from 177 to 242 across publishers between January and April 2020, but fell from 50 to 35 within Reuters.

papers.title: The Private Production of Safety Outside Options and the Burden of Protection
papers.summary: Protective interventions are typically evaluated by their ability to prevent harm. Yet protection also raises a distinct question: who bears the burden of adjusting to violence? I examine this allocation of protective adjustment using four randomized interventions in the United States. An offer of permanent housing assistance increases separation from a baseline partner combined with stable independent housing by 12.52 percentage points. Assignment to active police-response protocols reduces observed victim-only departures and increases suspect-only departures. Assignment to an emergency protection order increases documented directions for suspects to leave. These findings reveal two margins of the same allocation problem: housing assistance expands victims' ability to establish an independent residence, while enforcement shifts displacement obligations toward suspects. Protective policies thus shape not only the opportunities for safety, but also the distribution of the costs required to achieve it.

papers.title: Complying with Cybersecurity Legislation: NIS2 Challenges and Industry Case Study
papers.summary: Given the ever-increasing dependency on interconnected digital systems, cybersecurity has become a major concern. To protect markets and societies, governmental entities are developing legislation to enhance cyber resilience across sectors, introducing new technical and legal requirements. The NIS2 Directive, a revised version of the European-wide cybersecurity legislation, entered into force on 16 January 2023. Member States were required to adopt and publish transposing measures by 17 October 2024 and apply them from 18 October 2024. Specific obligations for essential and important entities are set out in national legislation. At the same time, other organizations, while not legally bound, seek to improve their cybersecurity maturity in alignment with EU-wide advances, for which NIS2 serves as a key reference. This paper presents the work conducted within a large European enterprise to align itself with the NIS2 Directive, focusing on how organizations can analyze and interpret its provisions to drive concrete technical and organizational improvements. A systematic methodology is applied to frame the company within the NIS2 context, identify relevant requirements, and derive actionable measures. Beyond outlining the technical steps taken, the work highlights the challenges of translating legislative requirements into practical implementations, emphasizing the use of existing IT resources while accounting for key legal aspects. The paper concludes with a discussion and reusable artifacts addressing critical areas such as Supply Chains and Third Parties and Zero-Trust Principles, illustrating how legislative instruments such as NIS2 can be translated into practical mechanisms to strengthen cybersecurity strategies.

papers.title: Hint of universality in $α$-cluster nuclei
papers.summary: The empirical ground-state energies of the $α$-cluster nuclei are placed on the universal function that governs $N$-boson systems with a shallow state. The data fall on the finite-range-corrected universal curve, suggesting Efimov-type universality. No excited states, transition strengths, radii, or cluster geometries enter the analysis; the nuclei are treated as $N$ structureless bosons. A zero-shape $α$-$α$ Bargmann potential, describing the $^{8}$Be resonance, provides the pairwise interaction with no shape freedom. Simple three- and four-body forces, each a single Gaussian in the hyperradius, are fitted to $^{12}$C and $^{16}$O; microscopic calculations for $^{20}$Ne and $^{24}$Mg ($N=5,6$) follow as parameter-free predictions. A compact $0^+_2$ state near the Hoyle energy emerges in $^{12}$C without being targeted by the fit.

papers.title: CocoonBench: Can Multilingual Search Agents Escape Language Information Cocoons?
papers.summary: Multilingual search agents can access the global Web, yet may remain trapped in a language environment with insufficient evidence; we refer to this failure as a language information cocoon. However, existing search benchmarks largely operate within a single language, especially English, overlooking entity connections across multiple languages. We introduce CocoonBench, a benchmark that evaluates whether multilingual search agents can escape such language information cocoons. CocoonBench mines answer-centered relational paths from a frozen Wikidata-derived graph and selects clue sets that are individually necessary and jointly identify a unique answer. Using language-specific entity names, it records each task's minimum language cover, removes direct identifiers, and renders each task as matched prompts in three languages together with its construction certificate and provenance. Across 10 state-of-the-art models, mean accuracy on CocoonBench ranges from 33.8% (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) to 69.7% (Claude-Opus-4.8), leaving even the strongest system below 70%. The same construction certificates support path-aligned trajectory analysis, enabling diagnosis of model failures in language routing, evidence-path recovery, and answer use. The result shows that escaping a language cocoon requires more than switching languages: successful cross-lingual search depends on both covering the correct languages and connecting the evidence found across them.

papers.title: Detecting Frame Dragging Effect with Next-Generation Spaceborne Clocks in a LEO-DRO Satellite Configuration
papers.summary: Our approach employs a satellite constellation comprising one satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO) and one satellite in distant retrograde orbit (DRO). This configuration is designed to enhance the sensitivity to the Earth's rotation-induced frame-dragging signal while providing a stable and gravitationally isolated frequency reference. We derive a complete relativistic formulation for the frequency comparison between LEO and DRO, incorporating the post-Newtonian metric, higher-order Earth multipoles, lunar and solar tidal potentials, and the gravitomagnetic vector potential. The frame-dragging signal is of order $10^{-20}$, a level that is becoming increasingly accessible with next-generation optical clocks. Recent advances in zero-dead-time strontium optical lattice clocks have demonstrated a fractional frequency instability of $2.9\times10^{-19}$ at an averaging time of 20,000~s, with an estimated one-day stability of $2.5\times10^{-19}$. With continued advances in clock stability, achieving fractional-frequency sensitivity at the $10^{-20}$ level appears feasible in the near term, potentially enabling the direct measurement of a frame-dragging signal of the same order. Such a measurement would constrain Earth's gravitomagnetic field, enabling future investigations of gravitomagnetic effects on Einstein clock synchronization.

papers.title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
papers.summary: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens. Their tokenizer must therefore preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semantic-enhanced tokenizers may lose acoustic detail, whereas acoustic-oriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that makes language modeling harder. Unified tokenizers combine both, but representing acoustic detail and linguistic content within a single feature space can cause interference between the two objectives, and existing approaches typically align acoustic representations to fixed semantic targets from a frozen teacher. We propose Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization (BiSAT), a unified tokenization framework with separate acoustic and semantic branches aligned by a shared-index mechanism. This design learns acoustic and semantic representations in separate continuous spaces while producing a single discrete code sequence, and it jointly optimizes both encoders without relying on fixed semantic teacher targets. Based on BiSAT, we develop BiSAT-TTS, a zero-shot text-to-speech system comprising an autoregressive text-speech LM and a conditional flow-matching acoustic decoder. Reconstruction, downstream understanding, and diagnostic analyses show that BiSAT effectively preserves semantic and acoustic information in the code stream, performs well on in-the-wild and out-of-domain speech, and learns complementary codebook representations. The frozen-code understanding results also support its feasibility and potential for code-based reward modeling in reinforcement learning post-training. BiSAT-TTS performs comparably to state-of-the-art speech LM-based TTS baselines with less training data, further supporting BiSAT's effectiveness for speech language modeling. The audio demos are available at https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo.

papers.title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation
papers.summary: Video-to-audio generation synthesizes sound that matches a video in content and timing, with applications ranging from film post-production to live streaming, games and interactive world models. Interactive applications receive video continuously and need the sound to follow it in real time, yet most existing video-to-audio models are bidirectional and must observe an entire clip before producing any sound. We propose LiveAudio, a streaming video-to-audio framework that generates high-quality and synchronized audio in real time while the video is playing. In contrast to prior streaming models trained from scratch, LiveAudio converts a bidirectional model into a streaming generator so as to build on its audio quality and synchronization. LiveAudio generates audio block by block, and each block depends only on the video that has already been played. The streaming generator is obtained from the bidirectional model through progressive causal fine-tuning and distillation, so that each block needs only a few sampling steps. Experiments on VGGSound show that LiveAudio outperforms existing streaming models in audio quality and synchronization, and surpasses the bidirectional model it starts from in synchronization. On a single A100 GPU, it runs in real time with a real-time factor of 0.79 and a time to first frame of 143 ms. Audio samples are available at https://streamaudio.github.io.

papers.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
papers.summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to $\sim 7 \%$. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.

papers.title: Hard to Translate, Harder to Detect: Human Analysis Remains Essential in AI Meme Translation
papers.summary: We present a dataset and evaluation setup for a problem in creative machine translation: translating culturally loaded passages that carry much of a text's meaning and humor that may depend on subtle or implicit discourse. We study Soviet comedy quotations that function as memes in Russian-language communication. Off-the-shelf difficulty estimators do not find these passages; current models searching the web find most but not all of them, but their own analyses of the difficulty do not help translation as well as a human-validated one. Given a brief human-validated analysis of why each passage is difficult, older models improve modestly; the strongest current translators (GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5) improve more, and in human evaluation GPT-6 Sol comes close to the approved references on most films. Newer models have thus become much better at using such an analysis while still not reliably producing it themselves. We release (1) a dataset of five films' Russian subtitles with their audience-selected culturally salient passages, human-validated analyses, and reference translations (into English, Galician, and Spanish), together with every full-film LLM translation and evaluation produced in this study; and (2) an item-level MQM-style evaluation protocol that measures translator and evaluator noise to set the number of runs the evaluation needs, and whose automatic version tracks human judgment of these passages, which reference-free neural metrics do not, whether they score the whole text or the passages alone.

papers.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
papers.summary: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. Electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the Weyl charge, and the Euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. For every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the Cauchy horizon. Finally, once the higher-derivative Weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and Laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.

papers.title: Bayesian sequential decision-making for adaptive early warning of bridge failure risk
papers.summary: As a critical functionality of structural health monitoring (SHM) systems, early warning of increased bridge failure risk is essential for structural safety. However, traditional methods treat early warning merely as passive detection against a fixed safety limit and neglect evolving uncertainties and the economic consequences of decisions, leading to delayed alarms that increase the failure risk and hinder reliable and rational decision-making. This study formulates the early warning of increased structural failure risk as a sequential decision-making problem and develops a Bayesian framework for its solution. The presented framework unifies a probabilistic state transition model, an observation prediction model, cost models for early warning decisions, and a threshold-based decision strategy into a closed loop encompassing update, prediction, optimization, and decision execution. The structural state is updated iteratively via Bayes' theorem upon the arrival of new monitoring data, ensuring each decision is conditioned on the latest information. Through pre-posterior analysis over predicted future observations, the warning threshold is optimized by minimizing the expected total cost, which explicitly balances structural failure risks against warning response costs. In this way, the warning paradigm is shifted from passive detection to proactive decision-making, with the warning threshold adaptively updated as uncertainties and costs evolve. The framework was verified via two bridge case studies covering typical scenarios that lead to increased structural failure risk, including steel truss member fracture and stay cable rupture. Results demonstrate that warning decisions can be triggered in a timely and effective manner before severe consequences occur.

papers.title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL
papers.summary: When RL learns from the reactions of many users, the policy usually cannot see what each user wants. We ask what it learns from users who privately want validation: to validate them alone (targeting), or to lower its bar for endorsing everyone (a threshold shift). We answer this in one setting, empathetic RL against LLM-simulated users (RLVER, GRPO, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): we vary only the share of validation-seeking users (0--50%; RLVER's default: 24.6%) and evaluate on 1,000 Reddit AITA posts with community fault verdicts. The policy shifts its threshold. Endorsement of at-fault posters rises by 3--4 percentage points per 10 points of share; without such users the Qwen model stays at base, and the effect persists at matched KL and under a goal-blind reward. Signal-detection analysis shows that the criterion for endorsing falls while discrimination between at-fault and not-at-fault posters does not decline. An explicit request to be told if one is wrong gives no measurable protection: at-fault posters who make it receive nearly the same rise as those who do not (+0.11 vs. +0.13). When the goal is stated during training, the policy instead largely targets, endorsing seekers regardless of fault. Standard sycophancy and empathy benchmarks miss the shift; five of six usable released empathetic-RL checkpoints also endorse at-fault posters who ask for honesty more than their base models, though a pre-registered prediction for two held for only one. The user mix is a training hyperparameter to audit and report.

papers.title: Sequential Monitoring of Image Streams Using Energy Statistics
papers.summary: Sequential monitoring of image data is a high-velocity, high-dimensional big data problem in statistics and machine learning, with wide applications in manufacturing industries, satellite imaging, medical diagnostics, and remote sensing. This is a challenging task because image intensity functions are often contaminated by noise and contain discontinuities and other complicated spatial structures. In the literature, a vast majority of image-monitoring methods rely on changes in image intensity values to detect out-of-control images. However, such approaches are often unreasonable in applications where insignificant changes in image contrast or background intensity should not indicate an out-of-control image as long as the boundaries of the image objects remain unchanged. In this article, we propose a nonparametric Phase II image-monitoring procedure based on energy distance that directly monitors changes in the distribution of image boundaries. The proposed method constructs a moving-window energy-distance-based control statistic by comparing the distribution of recently observed image boundaries with that of a fixed in-control reference sample. The central idea behind the proposed boundary-based approach is twofold: first, to reduce the dimensionality of high-resolution images by retaining relevant edge information, and second, to provide a robust monitoring procedure that is less sensitive to insignificant smooth changes in image intensity. The proposed construction offers a computationally efficient distributional approach to image monitoring without requiring a parametric model for out-of-control images. Theoretical justifications and superior performance in numerical comparisons ensure that the proposed control chart can be useful to many researchers and practitioners.

papers.title: Construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor of the Skyrmion coupled to additional dynamical degrees in the large-$N_c$ expansion
papers.summary: We formulate an order-by-order construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor (EMT) in the large-$N_c$ expansion of the model where the Skyrmion is coupled to additional dynamical fields. We show that, expanding the equations of motion and the EMT in powers of $1/N_c$, the inclusion of the backreaction to the Skyrmion from the additional fields is essential for achieving the conservation law of the EMT, which is contrasted with the fixed-background approximation where the effects of backreaction are neglected. We apply the construction to the model for hyperons based on the Callan-Klebanov bound-state approach, where the antikaon is bound to the Skyrmion, to obtain the EMT up to next-to-leading order of the $1/N_c$ expansion. We explicitly show that the divergence of the EMT from the backreaction for the Skyrmion exactly cancels that of the kaon to achieve the conservation of the total EMT. We find that the conserved EMT gives a negative hyperon D-term whose magnitude is smaller than that of the nucleon D-term and radii of gravitational form factors for the hyperon smaller than those for the nucleon, which implies that the hyperon is more compact than the nucleon.

papers.title: An Alphabet-Size Bound for the Information Bottleneck Function
papers.summary: The information bottleneck function gives a measure of optimal preservation of correlation between some random variable $X$ and some side information $Y$ while compressing $X$ into a new random variable $W$ with bounded remaining correlation to $X$. As such, the information bottleneck has found many natural applications in machine learning, coding and video compression. The main objective in order to calculate the information bottleneck is to find the optimal representation on $W$. This could in principle be arbitrarily complicated, but fortunately it is known that the cardinality of $W$ can be restricted as $|{\cal W}|\leq|{\cal X}|+1$ which makes the calculation possible for finite $|{\cal X}|$. Now, for many practical applications, e.g. in machine learning, $X$ represents a potentially very large data space, while $Y$ is from a comparably small set of labels. This raises the question whether the known cardinality bound can be improved in such situations. We show that the information bottleneck function can always be approximated up to an error $δ(ε,|{\cal Y}|)$ with a cardinality $|{\cal W}| \leq f(ε,|{\cal Y}|)$, for explicitly given functions $δ$ and $f$ of an approximation parameter $ε>0$ and the cardinality of ${\cal Y}$. Finally, we generalize the known cardinality bounds to the case were some of the random variables represent quantum information.
papers.comment: 6 pages. This paper was originally published in the proceedings of IEEE ISIT 2020 and has now been made available on arXiv
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory (ISIT), pp. 2383-2388

papers.title: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Deep Reinforcement Learning for QoS-Aware AI-RAN Configuration
papers.summary: Configuring radio access networks (RANs) for heterogeneous services requires coordinating radio parameters whose effects on throughput, delay, and reliability are closely coupled and evolve over different timescales. This paper presents a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for joint, QoS-aware RAN configuration that aligns the learning structure with the real-time, near-real-time, and non-real-time control loops of O-RAN that are also adopted by AI-RAN. Three proximal policy optimization agents jointly select per-user modulation and coding schemes, user-to-bandwidth-part (BWP) assignments, per-BWP transmit power, numerology, and BWP bandwidth weights, at three timescales. The agents share a QoS-aware objective combining throughput demand satisfaction with delay and reliability penalties. We extend ns-3 5G-LENA and integrate it with Ray RLlib through ns3-ai to support the required radio controls, network observations, and hierarchical policy execution. We evaluate the agents' performance in a nine-cell downlink network with inter-cell interference, varying user populations, and mixed URLLC, gaming, conversational-video, and video-streaming traffic. Compared with the baseline 5G-NR RAN, our trained hierarchical DRL agents substantially reduce URLLC and conversational-video delays, lower the residual block error rate, and prevent the near-starvation of the weakest flows, trading off slightly lower throughput for high-rate video streaming under capacity-limited conditions.

papers.title: Synthetic Twins: Closing the Gap Between TTS Test Sets and Real Recordings in Turkish ASR Evaluation
papers.summary: Speech synthesized by text-to-speech engines is a low-cost substitute for recorded test sets in automatic speech recognition, yet an off-the-shelf synthetic test set is worth only a few dozen real recordings for estimating the real error rate of a recognizer. This paper examines which properties of real recordings are missing from synthetic speech and how much of the gap can be closed. For 507 Turkish Common Voice recordings, synthetic twins are built: a ladder of synthetic copies that adds, one factor at a time, the pitch of the speaker, a clone of the same speaker, the real recording channel and the speaking rate. At each step, the agreement between ASR behaviour on the copy and on the real recording is measured. Across three zero-shot cloning engines and panels of six and 19 recognizers, the speaker clone is the step that improves agreement on which sentences are hard, raising the Spearman correlation from .41 to .55 for Chatterbox. Matching the channel or adding generic noise corrects the error level when the synthetic speech is easier than real speech. The twin with the highest worth is equivalent to 70 to 122 real recordings, depending on the recognizer panel, compared with about 9 for a stock voice. The findings replicate on VoxForge, a second corpus in which speaker identity is known rather than inferred: the clone raises sentence agreement from .31 to .50 and the worth from 8 to about 50 recordings. Agreement on which sentences are hard is distinct from agreement on how hard they are. The paper concludes with a practical recipe and a reporting checklist for synthetic ASR test sets.

papers.title: Mass-conservative and phase-consistent transport of phase-confined scalars in front tracking
papers.summary: In front-tracking multiphase-flow simulations, the Lagrangian front defines the interface geometry and phase regions, while phase-confined scalars are transported independently on a fixed Eulerian mesh. This separation can make the scalar inconsistent with the tracked interface: even a conservative high-order scheme smears the scalar across the interface, leaks it into the other phase and distorts near-interface concentrations despite conserving total mass. We present a transport method that maintains consistency between the scalar and the tracked front while preserving global mass conservation. Instead of the cell-averaged concentration, the method transports the phase-averaged concentration, which is smooth across the interface. This concentration is obtained by dividing the cell-averaged concentration by the phase fraction, extended linearly across the interface and advected. The cell-averaged concentration is rebuilt by multiplying the transported concentration by the front's volume-preserving phase fraction. Because this rebuild can alter the total mass, a uniform shift of the phase-averaged concentration restores it. The method is compared with direct transport of the cell-averaged concentration by the same scheme in five three-dimensional cases: three drops (in translation, in a reversible vortex and with a localized source) and a rising bubble with and without dissolved surfactant. In the four cases without surfactant it reduces the error against the exact solution by more than a factor of ten at the finest resolution and converges faster for the drops. In the surfactant-laden bubble, direct transport leaks 5.5-24% of the surfactant into the wake, depending on resolution, whereas the proposed method keeps it in the bubble.

papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity
papers.summary: We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincaré inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and uniform distributions. More broadly, this work demonstrates that discrete, non-local dynamics, such as Hit-and-Run, can be made amenable to powerful analytical methods, such as variational hypocoercivity.

papers.title: Learn the Effects, Not the Examples: Implicit ICL via Attention Patching
papers.summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables language models to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations, but repeatedly including multiple examples increases context length and inference cost. Many existing implicit ICL methods encode demonstrations as fixed vectors, limiting adaptation of the intervention to individual queries and token positions. We propose Attention-Patching, an implicit ICL method that models contextual changes in self-attention outputs through task-specific updates to attention output projections. Using query-answer pairs processed with and without a fixed demonstration set, Attention-Patching fits layer-wise affine transformations from non-contextual attention representations to the demonstration-induced output changes. Across 12 classification benchmarks and four model families, Attention-Patching achieves higher average accuracy than the evaluated implicit ICL baselines while maintaining performance comparable to explicit ICL at near zero-shot inference cost. Further experiments on diverse generation tasks demonstrate its applicability to autoregressive multi-token generation.

papers.title: Coherence transfer under bounded channel capacity
papers.summary: We investigate quantum coherence transfer between two parties whose local reference bases are misaligned, under a constraint on the capacity of the quantum communication channel. Within the resource theory of coherence, we formulate the task as maximizing the coherence received by Bob when Alice is restricted to Maximally Incoherent Operations (MIO) in her local basis. We first analyze two single-shot protocols, based on direct and locally entangled transmission, and derive their phase-optimized coherence yields. We further investigate their performance when Bob's reference basis is unknown, averaging over uniformly distributed basis configurations. In the asymptotic regime, we exploit the reversibility of coherence under MIO to characterize achievable transfer rates in terms of Alice's initial coherence. For single-qubit transmission, we derive an analytical lower bound using pure-state conversions and identify a regime in which the optimal yield saturates the channel capacity.

papers.title: Power-Swing Blocking and Out-of-Step Tripping Scheme Using the Swing Center Voltage in Systems With Inverter-Based Resources
papers.summary: Misoperation of power-swing blocking (PSB) and out-of-step tripping (OST) schemes in distance relays is a critical concern in power systems with increasing penetration levels of inverter-based resources (IBRs). Recently, several papers have studied the impact of IBRs on conventional dual-blinder PSB/OST schemes. They highlight interoperability issues concerning fast power swings and unconventional impedance trajectories, and propose revised relay settings in attempts to deal with the problems. However, the blinder-based PSB methodology suffers from being dependent on the speed of the apparent impedance just as it crosses between the blinders. It is therefore important to consider alternative methods. This paper thoroughly analyzes the characteristics of the swing center voltage (SCV) and the impacts of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverters on its local estimation. Then, an SCV-based PSB/OST scheme is proposed, where the main PSB criterion can be tuned from simple system parameters. This is made possible by a separate PSB activation function. The OST scheme uses only one setting and is motivated from the analytical analysis of the SCV with IBRs. Extensive PSCAD/EMTDC simulations verify the performance of the proposed SCV-based PSB/OST scheme and how it overcomes limitations of blinder-based schemes with GFM and GFL inverters.

papers.title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
papers.summary: The quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architecture is a promising approach to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing, enabling flexible qubit interactions by transporting ions between dedicated trap zones. Programs for such systems require operations beyond conventional circuit primitives: ion shuttling, physical SWAPs, trap splitting and merging, and cooling. Motional excitation accumulated during transport increases the mean phonon number of ions and degrades the fidelity of the two-qubit Molmer-Sorensen gates. However, existing quantum error correction (QEC) simulation frameworks do not jointly track per-ion motional excitation and explicitly schedule cooling operations with their transport time and heating costs. We develop a full-stack software framework for QEC experiments and simulations on linear QCCD systems with a single ion species, comprising an intermediate representation (IR) supporting QCCD-native operations, a compiler that translates syndrome-extraction circuits into the IR, and a heating-aware noise-injection pipeline that generates noisy Stim circuits. The compiler updates the mean phonon number of each ion throughout the schedule, and the pipeline derives gate-dependent error rates from the tracked phonon states and per-ion timing, enabling the evaluation of finite-size logical-error scaling of the rotated surface code under transport- and heating-aware noise. We show that transport-induced heating prevents logical error rates from decreasing with increasing code distance under the evaluated conditions, and that indirectly cooling the ion pairs involved in two-qubit gates, by merging them with precooled coolant ions immediately before each gate, restores this decrease. By sweeping the duration and post-cooling mean phonon number of an abstract cooling instruction, we characterize their trade-off and identify the region in which logical-error scaling is maintained.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 8 figures + 6 page appendix with 6 additional figures. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Empirical Margin Sensitivity: An Interventional Neuron-Level Probe of Post-Trained Medical LLMs
papers.summary: Medical post-training raises benchmark accuracy, but accuracy does not show which internal components a model's decisions depend on, or whether components that support one benchmark also support another. We apply the weight-space intervention paradigm of ROME and MEMIT at the granularity of one MLP down-projection column. Our measurement, Empirical Margin Sensitivity (EMS), replaces each coordinate magnitude of a column by its mean while preserving the column's sign pattern and L1 scale, and records the resulting change in the logit margin between the correct option and its hardest-wrong competitor. This isolates the margin's dependence on a column's fine-grained coordinate structure while the column stays in place. We discover high-EMS columns (anchors) on MedQA in ten public checkpoints (four general-purpose bases and six medical post-trained variants) across the Gemma, Llama, Qwen, and AFM families, and measure the same columns on MedMCQA and PubMedQA. Mean-ablating each discovered anchor set lowers MedQA accuracy in all six post-trained models, by 6 to 28 points. In the two pure-SFT checkpoints, crushing anchors raises the PubMedQA margin on correctly answered items (negative EMS), and anchors with this property sit significantly deeper than the same model's other anchors; the four checkpoints trained with RL or mixed recipes show positive PubMedQA EMS and no significant depth shift. The depth association recurs in each of three held-out checkpoints. Because the checkpoints differ in data and pipeline as well as objective, we report these as per-checkpoint observations.

papers.title: The user who is not there: genealogy and critique of simulated users built with generative AI in UX testing
papers.summary: Usability testing depends on people, and people's time does not speed up at the pace that software production demands. Large language models (LLMs) now promise to remove people from testing by generating simulated users that browse websites, answer questionnaires and give interviews. This paper examines how academic research understands that promise. It combines a critical literature review with a genealogical reading that follows the simulated user from the cognitive models of the 1980s to current generative agents. The paper makes four claims. First, testing without the user is an old aim of human-computer interaction (HCI), and cost has always justified it. Second, the validity criterion for user models shifted from predictive precision to believability, and recent studies that return to precision report weak results. Third, simulated participants conflict with the values of academic research and with methods that treat participation as a political right, with Participatory Design as the limit case. Fourth, the Latin American literature found in this review uses generative AI to support expert inspection and contains no study of synthetic users. That gap leaves open questions about who gets represented and about research ethics regulation in Brazil. The paper closes with an agenda of open problems. As part of its method, it reports that the review itself used an LLM as research assistant, and it discusses what that implies.

papers.title: Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals
papers.summary: Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. When ions are pinned to prescribed candidate sites, choosing which sites to occupy to minimize the Coulomb energy is NP-hard in two and three dimensions; a finite-precision promise version is NP-complete. All ions are identical, the interaction is bare Coulomb repulsion, and the hardness is carried by the site positions alone. We extend a previous inverse-square reduction to the Coulomb interaction by deriving its angular law, including the quartic field term, and sharpening two estimates. The construction is an array of quadrupoles whose common monopole term cancels from energy differences between legal configurations. Its energy landscapes exhibit large barriers between nearly degenerate minima. Barrier trees resolve this structure, and simulated annealing becomes trapped above the ground state in the cube example. At laboratory parameters, with individually tunable well depths, the encoding survives numerically on a half-filled square lattice. For Doppler-cooled strontium ions, this requires stiff wells a few to tens of micrometers apart, as in electrode trap arrays.

papers.title: A Proposal for Multiplierless RLS Adaptive Filters with Implementation Complexity Constraint
papers.summary: The so-called sum-of-powers-of-two arithmetic has the advantage of using simple shift and thus avoiding multiplications operations. In this work, we provide a feasible RLS adaptive filter algorithm employing the SOPOT representation. This reduces the computational burden of the RLS algorithm. Therefore, leading to a reduction in the power consumption from a hardware implementation point of view, which is an important feature in the developing of smaller, lighter and more power-efficient portable devices.
papers.journal: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS), IEEE, Oct 2020, Seville, Spain. pp.1-5

papers.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
papers.summary: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

papers.title: Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood
papers.summary: Finite mixture regression is sensitive to gross residual outliers when component errors are modeled by Gaussian likelihoods. We propose a log-truncated likelihood for mixture regression.
